The role of a physiotherapist is unrelated to cognition in driving. Physiotherapists provide education and tools to optimize a patient’s mobility.

On the topic of elder abuse, which statement is true? Elder abuse is more common if the abuser is financially dependent on the elder patient. Elder abuse is less common if the patient is perceived as frail. Elder abuse in long-term-care facilities may in part be due to the currently legislated minimum caregivers-to-residents ratio of 1-to-8. When caring for elder patients, caregivers experience a high degree of stress, but this does not correlate to increased rates of elder abuse. Rates of elder abuse have remained constant over the past ten years. The correct answer is A. Elder abuse increases as frailty increases. There is currently no legislation on the ratio of caregivers to patients in long-term-care facilities. Caregiver burnout is definitely correlated with elder abuse, and rates of elder abuse have increased in the past ten years in pa

Which of the following is not a consideration when selecting a treatment for a patient? Availability of the therapy Clinical guidelines Patient’s own wishes Physician’s own wishes The correct answer is D. A physician’s own wishes should not be factored into patient care.

Which pair of individuals are expected to have identical health outcomes? A man and a woman of the same race and ethnicity with the same condition and same treatment regimen Two men of the same age with the same condition but different socioeconomic status Two women of the same age with the same condition, of the same socioeconomic status, receiving the same treatment All of the above None of the above The correct answer is E. There are many individual differences from the genetic level to the environmental level, and identical outcomes in treatment are rare.

True or False: All drugs have a pharmacological target. True False The correct answer is B. Some drugs don’t have a specific target, such as laxatives that irate the walls of our guts, or antacids which modify stomach pH.

In the presence of Drug B, Drug A cannot reach the maximal response regardless of dose. Which of the following is true? Drug B affects the efficacy and is a reversible competitive antagonist Drug B has no effect on the EC50 and is a noncompetitive antagonist Drug B affects the potency and is a reversible competitive antagonist Drug B binds to the orthosteric site and is a noncompetitive antagonist The correct answer is B. Drug B does not affect the EC50 (or potency), but does affect the maximum dose response (it has an effect on efficacy). This indicates a noncompetitive antagonist.

Which definition below, pertaining to pharmacodynamics, is incorrect ? A partial agonist binds to a receptor and results in an increased activity relative to the baseline. An inverse agonist binds to a receptor, resulting in a decreased activity relative to the baseline. An allosteric antagonist binds to the same binding site as the receptor agonist and decreases the activity of an agonist. Competitive antagonists increase the required concentration for an agonist to elicit its maximal effect. Noncompetitive antagonists reduce the efficacy (maximal effect) of an agonist but leave its potency unchanged. The correct answer is C. Allosteric inactivators bind to a location on the receptor that is different than the binding site.

Consider the dose response curve below for three different drugs. Which of the following statements is false ? Drug A is more potent than Drug B and C Drug C can be Drug B in the presence of a competitive antagonist Drug C can be a partial agonist Drug A can be Drug B combined with a non-competitive antagonist The correct answers are C and D. C: Drug C reaches the full response, so it is not a partial agonist. D: a non-competitive antagonist lowers the maximal response but does not change potency, so it could not turn Drug B into Drug A, which is more potent than B. If Drug C is a partial agonist, we woul

Heroin is a mu-opioid receptor agonist. A pharmacologist is studying the effect of a novel drug, BK-562, on heroin’s dose-response, and early studies have shown that BK- 562 reduces the potency of heroin. It was also noted by the pharmacologist that if the concentration of heroin is sufficiently large, there is no change in maximal effectiveness. Which of the following statements is false ? BK-562 could be a partial agonist for the mu-opioid receptor. BK-562 could not be a noncompetitive antagonist for the mu-opioid receptor. BK-562 could decrease the EC50 of heroin. BK-562 could be a competitive antagonist for the mu-opioid receptor. BK-562 could be an inverse agonist for the mu-opioid receptor. The correct answer is C. Reducing a drug's potency raises its EC50 - more drug is needed for half the maximal effect - so BK-562 could not decrease heroin's EC50. Reducing the potency of a drug has the effect of increasing its ED50 of a drug.

Which of the following is not a broad class of receptor that drugs can target? G protein-coupled receptor Intercellular receptor Enzyme-linked receptor Ligand-gated ion channel The correct answer is B. This is a made-up term - the fourth broad category of receptors in an intracellular receptor.

The first-pass metabolism effect refers to the phenomena that: Parenteral (IM, SC, IV) drugs are sometimes metabolized in extracellular spaces reducing the bioavailability Oral drugs are sometimes metabolized in the liver reducing the bioavailability Oral and Transdermal drugs are sometimes able to attain sustained release due to slowed metabolic degradation Most drugs are able to bypass metabolic degradation on their first pass in the body The correct answer is B. First-pass metabolism is when certain oral drugs are metabolized in the liver or digestive tract before absorption into the bloodstream, reducing the bioavailability (concentration of drug in circulation). Note, parenteral drugs may still be metabolized before achieving main

Which of the following statements is correct with regards to Drug Distribution? Hydrophilic molecules are more easily able to cross the blood brain barrier Drugs that have a high affinity to plasma proteins (e.g albumin) tend to distribute faster Lipid-rich areas of low vasculature like the fat and bone can act as a reservoir for the drug Areas of low metabolism like the kidney and liver receive the drug faster The correct answer is C. Lipophilic molecules are more easily able to pass the BBB. Drugs with low affinity to plasma proteins distribute faster, areas of high blood flow receive the drug faster.

What major purpose do Cytochrome P450 macromolecules play in pharmacokinetics? These enzymes mediate most oxidation/reduction reactions in phase 1 metabolism These transporters are key transporters in the absorption of drugs in the intestine These enzymes facilitate reactions that make the drugs more lipophilic and increase drug solubility These enzymes often participate in conjugation reactions in phase 2 metabolism The correct answer is A. Many Phase 1 metabolism reactions are performed by CYP450 enzymes, which reduce the lipophilicity and increase the hydrophilicity.

A patient’s intestinal bacteria is severely diminished. With regards to drug pharmacokinetics which process would be significantly affected? Drug Metabolism Enterohepatic recycling Biliary excretion i, ii i ii, iii i, ii, iii The correct answer is A. Intestinal bacteria play a large role in drug metabolism and process drug conjugates in enterohepatic recycling to reintroduce them into circulation.

Which statement on the topic of pharmacokinetics is true? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY. The first-pass metabolism refers to initial metabolism of a drug by the digestive system before entering systemic circulation All drugs administered intravenously will have a higher bioavailability than drugs administered orally Elevated blood concentrations of albumin will increase the delivery of lipophilic drugs to their target tissue Drugs entering the brain must be hydrophobic to pass the blood-brain-barrier. The most common routes of elimination are renal excretion and biliary excretion. The correct answer is A, B, E. Albumin allows for the transfer of lipophilic molecules in the bloodstream. Elevated albumin would sequester these lipophilic molecules and reduce delivery to target organs. While lipophilic drugs more easily pass through the blood-brain-barrier, drugs can also pass th

Which option does not accurately describe an advantage of a route of administration of drugs? An advantage of rectal application is that it can be used to administer medicine on an unconscious patient. An advantage of transdermal application is the prolonged release of medication. An advantage of sublingual application is its delayed absorption. An advantage of subcutaneous application is its prolonged effect. An advantage of intramuscular application is its suitability for oil-based drugs. The correct answer is C. The main advantage of sublingual application is its immediate (not delayed) absorption.

A physician wants to establish a minimum plasma level of 4 mg/L of Drug A but wants to ensure that plasma concentration does not surpass the toxic level of 8 mg/L. Drug A has a half-life of one day. Assuming a bioavailability of 1 (100%), which of the following routines would best achieve this given your knowledge of steady state concentration. What is the best prescription option available? Prescribe a 500 mg tablet to be taken once daily (produces a plasma concentration of 8 mg/L) Prescribe a 250 mg tablet to be taken once daily (produces a plasma concentration of 4 mg/L) Prescribe a 500 mg tablet to be taken once every 2 days Prescribe a 125 mg tablet to be taken once daily (produces a plasma concentration of 2 mg/L The correct answer is B. Prescribing a dose that leads to 4 mg/L will eventually lead to a minimum plasma concentration of 4 mg/L at which point taking another dose will not surpass the 8mg/L threshold.

A half-life of a drug is estimated to be about 2 days in the human body. It also has a very large range between ED50 and TD50. Which statement below is true? It would take about 3-5 days for the drug to reach state-state concentration if the drug is administered every day. The steady-state concentration will not be changed if the dosing interval is doubled but the daily amount of drug administered is the same. The therapeutic window changes if the dose is increased. The maintenance dose often precedes the loading dose to establish a high plasma concentration quickly. A patient treated with this drug would likely require rigorous analysis to avoid toxicity issues. The correct answer is B. As long as the total daily dose is the same, adjusting the frequency of doses will not affect the steady-state concentration of the drug. For this drug, steady-state would be achieved after 6-10 days (3-5 times the half-life). Since the therapeutic window is so large (i.e.,

You are seeing a new geriatric patient in your family clinic and assessing their current medications. Which of the following concerns you the most regarding their current medication regimen? The patient occasionally forgets to take his daily dose of a drug with a small therapeutic window. The patient occasionally forgets to take his daily dose of a drug with a large therapeutic window. The patient occasionally doubles their daily dose of a drug with a small therapeutic window. The patient occasionally doubles their daily dose of a drug with a large therapeutic window. The correct answer is C. The small therapeutic window means that too large of a dose may lead to toxicity issues.

Which is the most incorrect description of the corresponding letter of the STEPS acronym in prescribing medication? Safety – will my patient be harmed taking this medication? Tolerability – Will the patient suffer side effects taking this medication? Effectiveness – Is there evidence that this medication will help the patient? Pharmacology – will the patient suffer any adverse drug reactions with this medicine? Simplicity – is the dosage regimen as simple as possible to increase adherence? The correct answer is D. The P in the STEPS acronym stands for Price - will the patient’s insurance or benefits be able to pay for this medication? If not, will they be able to afford this medication?

Which of the following statements is true? Decreased kidney blood flow and glomerular filtration rate in the elderly can lead to decreased elimination of drugs Women are more prone to adverse drug events than men Increased body fat composition tends to decrease volume of distribution in medications A and B A, B, and C The correct answer is D. Increased body fat composition tends to increase volume of distribution of lipophilic drugs.

Which of the following is not a reason for drug-response variability among patients? A diet rich in grapefruit activates CYP3A4, increasing metabolism of some drugs. The health of the liver affects the metabolism of drugs. The health of the kidney affects the elimination of drugs and metabolites. Polymorphisms in the CYP2C9 genes change enzyme activity. Copy number variation of CYP450 enzymes affects drug metabolism. The correct answer is A. Grapefruit inhibits CYP3A4 in the small intestine, which decreases the metabolism of some drugs and increases their bioavailability.

Which of the following considerations in prescribing to your patients based on race, gender, age, or disease is incorrect? Female patients should be prescribed a lower dose of the sleeping medication, zolpidem. Asian patients should be prescribed larger doses than Caucasians of the cholesterollowering drug Rosuvastatin. Black patients with heart failure are likely to benefit from treatment with BiDil. Older patients should be prescribed smaller doses of diazepam than younger patients. Patients with kidney impairment should be prescribed smaller doses of drugs which are primarily excreted renally. The correct answer is B. Asian patients should initially be prescribed smaller doses of Rosuvastatin. In fact, the 5 mg table of rosuvastatin was made specifically for Asian patients.

Which of the following statements are inaccurate? Many drugs are developed based on a 70-kg Caucasian male of 35-55 years of age. Benefit and risk of therapy are informed by patient input. In accordance with WHO’s rational prescribing guidelines, setting a therapeutic objective is the first step. Different therapeutic drugs can be used for people of different ethnicities to treat the same disease The correct answer is C. The first step is determining the patient’s problem. Then, a therapeutic objective can me made.

A patient with coronary artery disease (narrowing/blocking of cardiac blood vessels) is hospitalized. The patient’s presentation is a contraindication for which of the following drugs Aprotinin, which promotes blood clotting Hydralazine, which promotes vasodilation Acetaminophen, a pain reliever Dulcolax, a laxative The correct answer is A. Giving a drug that promotes clotting to a patient with narrow blood vessels can lead to a blockage and harm the patient. A contraindication a condition which precludes prescription of a drug.

Which of the levels of government pay for the bulk of a Canadian’s drug plan? International Federal Provincial Municipal The correct answer is C. Approximately half of all drug costs are paid for by the provincial government. About one- quarter is paid for by insurance plans, and the remaining one-quarter is paid for out-ofpocket.

Which option incorrectly describes the Phase of clinical trials? Pre-clinical trials involve assessing efficacy and toxicity in animals. Phase I clinical trials involve about 20 healthy patients, usually men, to see how the drug affects humans Phase II clinical trials involve testing a compound on a select 100 patients with a condition. Phase III clinical trials involve patients – often in substantial numbers - to compare the drug being tested against the current standard of care. Phase IV clinical trials involve assessing cost-effectiveness and use in health care systems after release to the market. The correct answer is E. Phase IV is post-marketing surveillance: once Health Canada approves a drug, it keeps being watched for safety in the wider population (09 - Canada's Healthcare System). E describes it as a study of cost-effectiveness and health-system use, which is not what Phase IV is. A t

Allan is a healthy 41-year-old male who presents to your clinic for a periodic health encounter, which of the following will you NOT perform as his general practitioner? Conduct a thorough patient history, with a focus on risk factors Order an investigation for a complete blood count to assess the numbers and conditions of his blood cells and plasma proteins Screen for high cholesterol and diabetes Measure and evaluate his BMI The correct answer is B. Allan is healthy and is not presenting with symptoms or risk factors that suggests the need for a CBC (e.g. possible anemia).

Which of the following regarding risk factors is true: Sedentarism is not necessarily a risk factor for chronic diseases Hypercholesterolemia can lead to retinopathy Diabetes screening can be used as a part of the diagnostic criteria for diabetes All of the above Only B and C The correct answer is E. Sedentarism is always a risk factor for chronic diseases. During diabetes screening, a patient is considered diabetic when their FPG ≥ 7 mmol/L or A1C ≥6.5%.

You are collecting blood samples for a complete blood count (CBC), which is the correct tube to collect your samples in? Red top tube Purple top tube Green top tube Navy top tube The correct answer is B. From 06 - Adult Screening - Diagnostic Pathway (its tube-colour chart; and 07 - Introduction to Laboratory Medicine). The chart pairs the lavender (purple) K2 EDTA tube with the full blood count (FBC/CBC), along with HbA1c and ESR. 07 names collecting the proper specimen typ

Which of the following regarding lab test performance is correct? The predictive value of a test is affected by the prevalence of the disease in the population The ROC curve is a plot of the specificity against sensitivity The higher the area under the curve, the worse the diagnostic test Specificity of a test is used to describe the presence of a disease. The correct answer is A. The ROC curve is a plot of the false positive rate (1-specificity) and true positive rate (sensitivity). The higher the area under the curve, the better the diagnostic test. Specificity of a test is used to describe the absence of a disease.

Which of the following is NOT a reason for Choosing Wisely? There are more than 1 million potentially unnecessary medical tests and treatments each year Choosing wisely is a form of rationing medical resources. Positive predictive value decreases with decreasing pretest probability. A majority of the cascades of care after incidental findings caused harm to the patient or the physician. The correct answer is B. From 08 - Choosing Wisely Review (and 07 - Introduction to Laboratory Medicine). The lecture defines Choosing Wisely as appropriate utilization , balancing underutilization and overutilization . Rationing withholds care to save resources, which is underuse: the reverse of wh

Which of the following contributes to the increase in potentially unnecessary testing: The Silo effect Increases lab revenue Fear of malpractice by physician Patient attitude of “more is better” All of the above The correct answer is E. From 08 - Choosing Wisely Review. The lecture's “Why Choosing Wisely?” table gives drivers of over-testing at every level, and each option is one of them: A the silo effect - health systems (culture and historical practice). B revenue - labs. C malpractice fear - physicians,

Which one of the following conditions would trigger the release of natriuretic hormones: Decrease in ECF volume Increase in ECF volume Decrease in osmolarity Increase in osmolarity. The correct answer is B. Natriuretic hormones are released when the atria or ventricles is stretched, which is when there is increase in ECF volume.

Which of the following is the fastest response to a drop in blood pressure: RAAS pathway Decrease in GFR Cardiovascular reflexes Release of aldosterone The correct answer is C. From 02 - Introduction to Blood Pressure Regulation. The lecture splits blood pressure control in two: the autonomic nervous system is the short-term, rapid response , and hormonal mechanisms are the long-term, slow one. A fall in pressure unloads the high-pressure barorecep

During dehydration which results in an increase in osmolarity and a decrease in ECF volume, which of the following is TRUE i) Hypothalamus triggers the release of ADH from the posterior pituitary to increase water reabsorption from the kidneys ii) Aldosterone activity will increase due to stimulated release by angiotensin II iii) RAAS will be triggered, leading to activation of angiotensin II iv) Vasoconstriction All of the above i,ii, iii i,iii,iv i,ii, iv The correct answer is A. All four happen: hyperosmolality releases ADH (i), low volume activates RAAS (iii), and angiotensin II both raises aldosterone (ii) and causes vasoconstriction (iv). When the body is experiencing hyperosmolar dehydration, there is priority in restoring osmolarity over restor

Which of the following is true: i) Heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature and blood pressure are the four primary vital signs ii) Most of the blood volume is distributed in the veins iii) Males sometimes have higher blood pressure than females iv) Total peripheral resistance is partially related to the blood volume v) The heart is only innervated by the sympathetic nervous system. All of the above i,ii, iii i, iii i,ii, iii, iv, i,iii,v The correct answer is B. The heart is innervated by both the SNS and PNS. From 02 - Introduction to Blood Pressure Regulation (and 06 - Adult Screening - Diagnostic Pathway for vitals). Statement by statement: i - HR, RR, temperature and BP are the classic vitals; every option includes i, so the que

Which of the following is true regarding blood vessel control: At rest, the SNS does not fire action potentials to the blood vessels SNS and PNS both innervate the arterioles, SNS directly causes vasoconstriction, and PNS directly causes vasodilation Tonic activity refers to the increase firing of action potentials from the SNS, resulting in activity of the blood vessels The SNS regulates both vasoconstriction and vasodilation The correct answer is D. The arteriole is only innervated by the SNS. The SNS causes both vasoconstriction and vasodilation by changing the tonic activity of the vessels.

Al comes to your psychiatry clinic with the following symptom clusters: avoidance, worried, impaired concentration, catastrophizing, and insomnia. These symptoms best correspond to which of the following mental disorders: Depressive disorder Bipolar disorder Anxiety disorder Obsessive-compulsive disorder. The correct answer is C. From 09 - Approach to Anxiety and Stress. The lecture's symptom-cluster tables sort each symptom into a sphere and a disorder. Avoidance (behavioural), worry (emotional) and catastrophizing (cognitive) belong to the anxiety cluster; impaired concentration and insomnia appear

Which of the following regarding the GAD-7 is true: A score of 5 on the GAD-7 is the cut-off for mild anxiety A score of 12 can be used to diagnose anxiety disorder The GAD-7 is only used to screening general anxiety disorder and has a low specificity and sensitivity for other anxiety disorders, such as panic disorder, and social anxiety disorder. The GAD-7 asks questions regarding the patient experiences in the past month. The correct answer is A. A score of 10 is taken as a cut off for moderate anxiety, but further evaluation is recommended when the score is over 10. The GAD-7 is also moderately good for screening panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, and PTSD. The GAD-7 asks questions regarding the patient experi

What is the first thing you do when you wish to order an investigation for your patient: Understand the correct steps to obtain sample Make a requisition with the lab Explain the investigation to the patient and obtain their consent Tell the patient and then order the investigation The correct answer is C. From 10 - Approach to Abnormal Test Results. The informed-consent section opens with the point: any test can find something bad, so the patient must understand what they are undergoing and what could result, and it is ultimately up to the patient whether to proceed. Explanat

Which of the following situations involves a breach in patient confidentiality: Your 12 year old patient wishes for her mom to accompany her throughout her visit and you didn’t ask the mom to leave while disclosing her blood test results Your patient with severe Alzheimer’s dementia is still driving every day to pick up their grandchildren from school. You discuss your legal obligations with the patient and report this to the Ministry of Transportation As their general practitioner, you referred your patient to a specialist and share their medication record with the specialist. You tell your colleague that your patient, Sally Baker, presents with a challenging case and wish to have them share their insight on approaching this case. The correct answer is D. Its ok to share with your colleagues a particularly challenging case, but don’t disclose information that can reasonably lead to the identity of the patient.

Which of following contributes to the highest sources of errors: Preanalytical Analytical Post-analytical They contribute almost equally The correct answer is A. From 07 - Introduction to Laboratory Medicine. The lecture states that most laboratory errors occur in the pre-analytical phase - everything that happens before the analyser measures the sample: wrong sample type, wrong order of draw, under-filled tubes, tubes not mixed afte

Which of the following is FALSE: It is pre-analytical error when the lab forgot to aliquot the samples before testing Mixing patient samples can result in patient death The last step to approaching an abnormal lab test is to consult a lab professional for insight Blood samples used to glucose measurements can’t be left out for too long The correct answer is C. The last step is considering the abnormal results could be correct.

All of the following are reversible adaptations a cell may undergo in response to changes in their environment, EXCEPT: Atrophy Apoptosis Hyperplasia Hypertrophy Metaplasia The correct answer is B. Atrophy, hyperplasia, hypertrophy, and metaplasia are all reversible adaptations to cell stress. Apoptosis is a form of cell death and is irreversible.

Which of the options below is a mechanism of cell injury? Mitochondria damage resulting in increased reactive oxygen species Entry of Ca2+ into the cell causing increased mitochondria permeability and activated of intracellular enzymes. Membrane damage causing leakage of cellular contents Protein misfolding and DNA damage All of the above The correct answer is E. All of the options listed are mechanisms of cell injury. Following these injuries, if cell death does not occur by apoptosis, it may lead to cancer.

Which of the options below correctly lists the order of the inflammatory response? Recruitment > Recognition > Regulation > Removal > Resolution Recruitment > Recognition > Removal > Regulation > Resolution Recognition > Removal > Recruitment > Regulation > Resolution Recognition > Recruitment > Removal > Regulation > Resolution Recognition > Recruitment > Regulation > Removal > Resolution The correct answer is D. From 12 - Adult Screening and Preventative Care Principles. The lecture runs the inflammatory response as the 5 Rs , and the order follows the logic of the response: Recognition of the offending agent by host cells and molecules → Recruitment of leukocytes and plasma protein

Which of the following is true about the interaction of the cardiovascular system with the respiratory system? Oxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle to the lungs for gas exchange Deoxygenated blood from the systemic circulation will undergo gas exchange at the lungs before returning to the heart. Oxygen is removed from the blood and carbon dioxide is added to the blood during gas exchange Unlike most arteries, the pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood to the lungs The correct answer is D. Deoxygenated blood from the systemic circulation is returned to the right side of the heart through the superior and inferior vena cava. This blood is transported to the lungs via the pulmonary arteries. At the lungs, gas exchange occurs: oxygen is added to the blood and car

Where is CO2 removed from the tissues and added to the blood? GI tract Skeletal Muscle Heart muscle (via coronary circulation) Lungs A, B, C A, B, D B, D A, B, C, D The correct answer is E. Working tissues - the gut, skeletal muscle and the heart - add CO 2 to the blood; the lungs take it out. All tissues participate in gas exchange, expelling waste CO2 produced via cellular respiration into the blood for transport into the lungs. At the lungs, deoxygenated blo

Which of the following correctly states a difference between a generic somatic nerve pathway and a somatic reflex arc? The generic somatic nerve pathway receives sensory information from the leg through the ventral ramus In the reflex arc, the general sensory afferent synapses on an interneuron in the dorsal grey horn. In the reflex arc, general motor efferents innervating the leg travel through the ventral root In the generic somatic nerve pathway, the spinal nerve contains both sensory and motor information. In the reflex arc, cell bodies of the general sensory afferents are located in the dorsal root ganglion. The correct answer is B. This is one of the differences between the generic somatic nerve pathway and the reflex arc. The result of the answer choices are similarities between both pathways.

It is Monday morning and you are relaxing while reviewing the COTW before class. You have just finished breakfast and are digesting to give you energy for the morning ahead. Which pathway would stimulate your stomach to start digesting your breakfast? Sympathetic pathway 1 Sympathetic pathway 2 Sympathetic pathway 3 Sympathetic pathway 4 Parasympathetic pathway from cranial nerves Parasympathetic pathway from the vagus nerve Parasympathetic pathway from pelvic splanchnics The correct answer is F. The parasympathetic nervous system (rest and digest) would be activated in this case rather than the sympathetic nervous system (fight or flight). The pathway that will innervate most of the abdominal viscera, including the stomach, is that from the vagus nerve.

What pathway will sympathetic innervation follow in order to activate sweat glands on your foot? The pre-synaptic neuron will leave the spinal cord at T1 and synapse at the same level on the sympathetic chain. The post-synaptic neuron will then travel down to the foot. The pre-synaptic neuron will exit the spinal cord at around L2-3, enter the sympathetic chain and descend to the appropriate lower limb ganglia where it will synapse. The post-synaptic neuron will travel to the foot. The pre-synaptic neuron will leave the spinal cord at S3 (the level of lower limb ganglia) and synapse with the sympathetic chain at the level. The post-synaptic neuron will then travel to the foot The pre-synaptic neuron will leave the spinal cord at L2-3 and synapse at the same level in the sympathetic chain with a splanchnic nerve, which will go to the foot. The correct answer is B. The sympathetic nervous system is thoracolumbar – meaning pre-synaptic fibers will only leave from T1-L2/3 (eliminates C). To reach beyond L2 or 3, presynaptic fibers would leave at that level of the spinal cord, then travel down the sympathetic chain to synapse on ganglia t

Which statement correctly describes equity? Giving everyone access to free post-secondary education Providing post-secondary school scholarships for people with low socioeconomic status. The correct answer is B. Equity is providing services to make sure everyone is on a level playing field – this could include giving scholarships to those who would otherwise not have the financial means to attend post-secondary school. Then both high and lower SES individuals would be able to attend

What are strategies the healthcare system can utilize to mitigate social determinants of health-related disparities? Promote cancer screening services Improve wait times to see a physician Ensure access to specialists All of the above The correct answer is D. all of those strategies could help reduce social determinants of health-related disparities in the Canadian healthcare system. Compared to the richest fifth, the poorest fifth are less likely to use cancer screening services, have fewer specialist visits, and experience long

Which of the following steps would you take to critically appraise screening and diagnostic test accuracy studies? How was the study designed? What are the results? Will these results help me care for my patients? Consult the STARD initiative and QUADAS-2 tool All of the above. The correct answer is E. You would want to consider all of these questions when reading a screening study.

The AGREE II instrument is the most useful instrument to assess guidelines. Which of the following is false regarding the AGREE II instrument? There are 23 questions organized into 6 domains The domains are dependent on each other Assess the methodological rigor and transparency in which a guideline is developed Domains include scope and purpose, stakeholder involvement, rigor of development, clarity of presentation, applicability, editorial independence. The correct answer is B. The domains are rated independently of each other. They are rated on a seven-point scale from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree).

All of the following are potential outcomes of screening, except: Possibility of creating and treating false positives Incorrectly missing those who had the condition (false negative) Reducing the likelihood of future events (e.g., screen for diabetes to prevent future heart attack) Increasing survival time The correct answer is D. We cannot say that screening tests improve survival time because of lead-time bias.

What is the most common reason why Canadians get sick? Wait times and poor access to healthcare Genetics Income, education, race, employment Environmental factors including air quality The correct answer is C. Factors related to your life make Canadians sick 50% of the time. These include: income, early childhood development, disability, education, social exclusion, social safety net, gender, employment, race, Aboriginal status, nutritious food, housing, and community belonging.

A tissue biopsy report indicates poor differentiation. What does this suggest? It has spread to the regional lymph nodes It highly resembles normal tissue It is growing rapidly It is considered low grade It is curable The correct answer is C. Differentiation does not reflect spread to lymph nodes or curability. Poor differentiation is usually high grade (associated with rapid growth) and does not resemble normal tissue.

A physical exam for a breast mass would NOT include: Identifying the quadrant of the mass Examination of nearby lymph nodes Identifying the contours of the mass Confirming if the mass is benign or malignant Determining if the mass is superficial or deep The correct answer is D. Confirming if the mass is benign or malignant cannot be done with a physical examination.

What is FALSE about cysts? It can be filled with air It has rough margins, meaning it is usually harmless It can collapse if the fluid in it is removed It is well demarcated from surrounding tissues It can be single or multiple The correct answer is B. Cysts have smooth margins. From 04 - Diagnostic Pathway for Breast Mass. A cyst is a sac of air, fluid or semi-solid that is well demarcated and well circumscribed with smooth margins . Rough or irregular edges are the malignant feature in the lecture's benign-vs-malignant t

When ordering tests, it is important to: Choose the most invasive option first to get it over with Order tests that rarely change management Try new testing options to better your learning experience Seek clarification if you believe a test was ordering unnecessarily Not discuss and educate the patients on the necessity of the tests The correct answer is D. It is better to seek clarification if you were unsure of the necessity for the test.

What is false regarding the stages of carcinogenesis? Initiation: Genetic alteration produces premalignant cells from healthy cells Transformation: premalignant cells proliferate Transformation: Second alteration produces malignant cells from premalignant cells Progression: Malignant cells to clinical cancer All are true The correct answer is B. Transformation is when a change causes cells to go from pre-malignant to malignant.

What is true regarding screening for colorectal cancer? FIT test every 5 years Specificity is 92.3% in detecting CRC Detects mammal heme Screening can only be done at doctor’s offices or hospitals FIT screening is for individuals between 50-74 years old The correct answer is E. FIT screening is the standard screening for CRC. It is every 2 years. Sensitivity is 92.3%.

What does the synoptic report in the pathology report include? Specimen Tumour grade Tumour margins Lymph node involvement All of the above The correct answer is E. Synoptic report includes all of the above. From 03 - Cancer Genetics (the surgical pathology report). The synoptic report is a concise, standardized checklist of the most important findings - the ones that predict outcome and guide treatment and further testing. The lecture

Which statement below is FALSE? Mutations in proto-oncogenes cause gain of function Mutations in tumour suppressor genes cause a loss of function BRCA1/2 mutations are autosomal dominant Tumour suppressor genes up-regulate the cell cycle Tumour suppressor genes mediate programmed cell death The correct answer is D. Tumour supressor genes inhibit the cell cycle. From 03 - Cancer Genetics. A tumour suppressor gene normally inhibits the cell cycle, slows proliferation or promotes apoptosis; cancer needs it lost (two hits, loss of function). Up-regulating the cycle describes an oncogene, s

What is false about breast cancer 5-year survival rate by stage? Stage 1 is 90% Stage 2 is 93% Stage 3 is 72% Stage 4 is 22% Stage 1 is 100% The correct answer is A. Stage 1 is 100% not 90%. Breast cancer 5-year survival falls with stage: essentially 100% at stage 1 , about 92-93% at stage 2, about 72-74% at stage 3 and about 22-23% at stage 4 (Canadian Cancer Society figures). The shape follows the staging logic in 02 - Approach to Neop

Which of the following is NOT a hallmark of cancer Evasion of apoptosis Sustained angiogenesis Dysplasia: abnormal pattern of growth Tissue invasion and metastasis None of the above The correct answer is C. Dysplasia is not cancer, but it may sometimes become cancer. It is NOT a hallmark of cancer

Match each presentation of a breast mass to the appropriate description. Abscess Collection of pus that is usually red, hot, swollen and tender Fibroad

Which of the following is TRUE regarding choosing investigations for a breast mass Mammography is used for screening and diagnosis, but it is a high energy form of radiograph Ultrasound is the most appropriate screening tool for detecting a breast mass for low risk patients. MRI is a useful screening tool for high risk populations and staging local disease. CT scans are a useful diagnostic tool for further workup of a breast mass finding. When there is suspicion of malignancy in breast tissue, fine-needle aspiration is the most appropriate investigation The correct answer is C. Mammography is a low energy form of radiograph. Ultrasounds is primarily diagnostic but can be used in screening high risk patients, as an alternative to MRI. CT scans are best performed post biopsy for cancer staging to check for metastatic disease, not for workup or screen

Which of the following patients should be screened for prostate cancer? Joe (age 32) a healthy patient, whose father and grandfather were diagnosed with prostate cancer at age 68 and 72 respectively. Will (age 65) a terminally ill patient with advanced heart disease Penn (age 57), a healthy black patient whose family history of prostate cancer is unknown B and C should be screened for prostate cancer because of their age Due to the potential harms of screening and overdiagnosis, prostate cancer screening is not recommended for any patient. The correct answer is C. Joe is too young for prostate cancer screening. Will is terminally ill and therefore screening would not be beneficial. Penn’s race and age may predispose him to higher risk of prostate cancer, therefore C is correct. E is incorrect because screening may be beneficial for th

Which of the following is LEAST indicative of hereditary cancer? Jillian was diagnosed with breast cancer at 52 and ovarian cancer at 61 Three members of John’s family (2 uncles, and his sister) developed lung cancer before age 65 without a significant smoking history Shelly’s sister, cousin and aunt have a history of ovarian and breast cancer Andrew and his brother, who were chronically exposed to benzene in their workplace, were diagnosed with leukemia. Ben was diagnosed with prostate cancer at age 46. The correct answer is D. Multiple primary cancers in one individual may be indicative of hereditary cancer (Jillian). Multiple individuals with lung cancer over several generations and no smoking history may indicate hereditary cancer (John). Shelly’s family history of ovarian and breast cancer may

Regarding genetic testing for cancer mutations, identify the TRUE statement Once a child is born in a family with a known pathogenic mutation, the child should undergo gene testing as soon as possible. The recommendation is that patients should undergo a comprehensive hereditary cancer panel regardless of their family history or risk level. When testing an unaffected individual at risk of having a genetic mutation, it is best to confirm the presence of a mutation in an affected family member first. Once a family member has tested positive for a mutation associated with cancer, other family members have to get tested to identify whether they are at risk The correct answer is C. It is not recommended to gene test children for mutations, unless there is a risk to develop the disease in childhood. Gene testing should be done based on patient characteristics and risk level (higher pre-test probability). C is the true statement. Patients have the choice

Rank each pathology report term from least (1) to most (5) malignant. The pairings: Terminology Rank (1 least to 5 most malignant) Atypia Present, Cannot exclude malignancy 3 Suspicion for Malignancy 4 Atypia Present, Favour Reactive 2 Positive for malignancy 5 - most malignant Negative for malignancy 1 - least malignant From 06 - Communication of the Pathology Report

Match each statement to the member of the cancer care team it describes. The pairings: Statement Team member Perform biopsies for cancer diagnosis and play a role in removal and cancer staging. General Surgeon Involved in cancer screening, symptom relief, counselling and referrals Primary Care Physician Provide education, resources and support to help patients and famili

Which of the following is not an example of instrumental activity of daily living? Ambulating Telephoning Preparing meals Cleaning the kitchen The correct answer is A. Basic activities of daily living are more simple activities, such as ambulating. Instrumental daily activities are more complex, and require higher levels of cognitive functioning, such as talking on the phone (B), preparing meals (C), and cleaning (D). Both BADLs and IADLs

Which of the following screen for depression? Cornell scale Patient health questionnaire 2 (PHQ-2) Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS) 4AT Both A, B, and C The correct answer is E. Both the Cornell scale and geriatric depression scale (GDS) are used to screen for depression. Patient health questionnaire 9 can also be used to screen for depression, not PHG-2 as stated in (B). Lastly, 4AT is used to screen for delirium.

What is the function of the frontal lobe? Sensation Speech production Language understanding Both B and C Memory The correct answer is B. The frontal lobe is responsible for motor function, speech production, executive function such as planning and problem solving. Sensation is controlled by the parietal lobe, and language understanding is controlled by temporal lobe. Memory is also controlled by the temporal

Which of the following are characteristics of Upper Motor Neuron (UMN) weakness? Muscle atrophy Spasticity Flexion plantar responses Normal tone The correct answer is B. Spasticity is influenced by Upper Motor Neuron (UMN) weaknesses. The remaining options, such as muscle atrophy, plantar responses, and normal tone are characteristics of Lower Motor Neuron weaknesses. An UMN weakness would be characterized by no significant atrophy, hyperact

Which of the following is an intrinsic cause of falls? Chronic illness Medications Alcohol Weather The correct answer is A. Chronic illness is an intrinsic cause of falling, whereas medications, alcohol and the weather are all external causes.

What is/are potential consequences of frailty? Death Worse hospital outcomes Dependency Longer hospital stays All of the above The correct answer is E. All of the above are consequences of frailty. Falls are the 5th leading cause of death in adults over 65, and are associated with injuries and disabilities, which can, in turn, lead to dependency, longer hospital stays and worse outcomes.

Which of the following correctly pairs the professional with one of their activities in working with the interdisciplinary team? Registered Dietician – ensure patients take their medicine using a dossette Pharmacist – adjust medicine based on renal dosing and drug-drug interactions Speech and Language Pathologist – teach American Sign Language Physiotherapist – assess and manage a wide range of issues, including mobility, cognition and safety The correct answer is B. Only the pharmacist is correctly paired with their role. Registered dieticians use dietary history, physical exams and lab results to assess an individual’s nutrition and risk, and work with them to ensure proper nutrition is maintained through various methods. A speech and

What does the DCAT not assess or provide? Span of attentional field Coordination of mental abilities Speed of attentional shifting Vehicle accessibility and seating The correct answer is D. The DCAT does NOT assess vehicle accessibility and seating. The DCAT assesses motor speed and control, span of attentional field, spatial judgement and decision making, speed of attentional shifting, coordination of mental abilities, and identification of driving situations.

Which of the following terms are not part of the 5Ms of geriatric care? Multi-complexity “Matters Most” Multi-laterality Mind Medications The correct answer is C. multi-laterality in this context does not exist. The five Ms of cognition are “Matters Most”, Mind, Mobility, Medications, and multi complexity.

As part of taking a social history in your comprehensive geriatric assessment, which of the following factors are important to gather information on? Supports: family, friends, neighbours, home care Travel: have they been outside of the country, if so how long Substances: alcohol, smoking, cannabis Immunizations: are they up to date on all their vaccinations A and D A, B and C A and C The correct answer is G. Supports and Substances are included in the social history of a geriatric assessment, however immunizations and travel are not covered here.

You wish to screen your patient for possible changes in their cognition. Which of the following cognitive testing offers the advantages of being fast and easy (should take about 7 minutes) while having the disadvantages of not being very sensitive for mild dementia nor of MCI, being copy righted, and being influenced by age and education? Mini-Cog Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) Rowland Universal Dementia Assessment Scale (RUDAS) The correct answer is B. The Mini-Mental state exam is roughly 7 minutes long, can be fast, is easy, and is disadvantaged in being copyrighted, not very sensitive, and being influenced by age and education.

An individual scores 30 on the MoCA. This is possibly suggestive of that individual having? Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) Dementia Alzheimer’s No cognitive symptoms of concern The correct answer is D. A score of 26 or higher is clear for the MoCA screen. This does not exclude any of the disorders from being a possibility, however getting a perfect score of 30 is likely to indicate being clear of these disorders.

Which of the following factors would constitute a biological factor that influences the maintenance of mental well being later in life? Socioeconomic issues Relationships Pain management Resilience The correct answer is C. pain management is classified as a biological aspect that can maintain mental well being. The others constitute more of the phycological and social maintainers.

Of the following risk factors, which are some of the risk factors for late life depression? Caregiver burnout Taking medications Personality type (avoidant or dependent personality) History of depression All of the above The correct answer is E. All of the above constitute risk factors for late life depression

Which are essential components of a preventative health visit for older adults? Acute issues/safety concerns MoCA Screening Basic Overall Risk Assessment (BOR) A and C The correct answer is E. The periodic health encounter for older adults runs on ALBUS : A cute issues and safety, L abs and vitals, B ook follow-up, U pdate profile, S creening. Acute issues (A) and screening (C) are both in it. The MoCA (B) is not: the lecture advises against screening asymptomatic

When should one screen for cholesterol? Both men and woman at age 40 every, 5 years Both men and woman at age 50 years every, 5 years For women starting at age 40 and men at age 50 every, 5 years For women starting at age 50 and men at age 40 every, 5 years The correct answer is D. From 02 - Periodic Health Encounter for Older Adults. Hypercholesterolemia screening starts at 40 for men and 50 for women , repeated every 5 years if risk factors do not change other than age, with risk estimated by the Framingham calculator. A - 40 is right for men only; w

Which of the following factors are not associated with healthy aging? Exercising regularly Sleeping 7-8 hours nightly Being socially disengaged Limiting alcohol consumption The correct answer is C. Typically the reverse is true, the extroversion and healthy social engagement are associated with longevity.

The following are associated with healthy aging except: Decreased ability to thermo-regulate Changes in body water/fat ratio Night vision declines Brain weight increases Maximal heart rate declines The correct answer is D. Brain weight DECREASES with age. From 01 - Healthy Aging vs. Disease. The normal changes of aging include variable loss of cortical and spinal cord neurons with a decrease in brain weight and functional reserve, so an increase is not part of healthy aging. A - normal: older

Which of the following statements regarding a physician’s approach to prescribing is TRUE? The WHO recommends administering treatment to narrow your differential when the causative pathology is unknown Palliative approaches specifically focus on end-of-life care Reading the primary literature is the most common way that clinicians utilise research in practice A patient that does not feel improvement following medication use does not necessarily mean that there was therapeutic failure The correct answer is D. Certain drugs, such as antihypertensives and diabetes medications, do not lead to subjective feelings of improvement when successful as a therapeutic agent.

When treating a patient using a prescription medication, which of these factors is the least important to consider: A comprehensive review of reported adverse events and their frequency of occurrence The alignment of the patient’s and providers goals of care How the number needed to treat (NNT) compares to the number needed to harm (NNH) of the standard treatment Use of prescription drugs, tablets, creams, inhalers, over-the-counter products and supplements The correct answer is A. While adverse events are important to consider, they are often not reviewed comprehensively. Instead, the most common and serious adverse events are discussed with the patient.

Which of the following is not a component of underpinning safe and rational prescribing, specifically when selecting a treatment? Analytical skills Clinical experience Foundational knowledge Understanding of individual variability The correct answer is D. Understanding individual variability is used in determining what dose of a therapeutic agent to give a patient. Thus, it is the least relevant of the options to treatment selection.

You would like to prescribe your patient amoxicillin. What must be included in every prescription? Drug, trade name, route of administration, dosing interval Drug, dose, length of treatment, adverse effects, dosing interval Drug, dose, route of administration, length of treatment, dosing interval Drug, chemical name, interactions, route of administration, length of treatment, dosing interval The correct answer is C. The chemical name, adverse effects and interactions are not included in a standard electronic prescription.

Which of the following statements regarding drug-receptor interactions is FALSE? The dose of a drug has a quantitative relationship with its effect until a ceiling effect is reached Drug-receptor binding exhibits specificity and selectivity The constitutive/basal activity of a receptor is reduced more by the binding of inverse agonists than by the binding of antagonists Termination of a drug response can be induced by dissociation or destruction of the drug-receptor complex The correct answer is B. Drug-receptor binding exhibits selectivity but not specificity. Oftentimes, a single drug can bind to all or most of the receptors in a receptor class.

Lindsay is a 31-year-old female patient who is administered isoproterenol to treat her bradycardia by increasing her heart rate. Later, she is also given propranolol, a competitive inhibitor of isoproterenol. Assuming that a full dose of isoproterenol will increase her heart rate by 100%, which of the following changes would be observed in her dose-response curve? The potency of isoproterenol will increase, requiring a lower concentration of isoproterenol to achieve a 50% increase in heart rate The efficacy of isoproterenol will decrease, worsening her bradycardia The potency of isoproterenol will decrease, requiring a higher concentration of isoproterenol to achieve a 50% increase in heart rate The potency and efficacy of isoproterenol will be unchanged The correct answer is C. Efficacy is not influenced by competitive inhibition; the dose-response curve would have the same EMAX. Potency decreases with competitive inhibition.

Which of the following is false regarding the Cytochrome P450 system? CYP enzymes catalyze the majority of phase I drug metabolic reactions There is little genetic variation in CYP genes among the general population CYP enzymes found in enterocytes can be induced or inhibited by components of the diet Redundancy among CYP enzymes means some drugs can be metabolized by more than one kind of CYP enzyme If a CYP enzyme that metabolizes Prodrug X is inhibited, then the plasma levels of Drug X will be lower than expected The correct answer is B. There is significant genetic variation among CYP genes. Polymorphisms in CYP genes largely explain the individual variability seen in response to medications. A particular drug may be toxic in poor metabolizers, while ultra-rapid metabolizers may have no response to the same

Which of the following is false regarding excretion? Drugs excreted via the biliary route of excretion tend to be amphipathic in nature One concern for breastfeeding mothers on medication is that drugs can be excreted into breastmilk The kidneys are responsible for the excretion of water-soluble drugs Once biliary-excreted drugs have entered the intestines they are destined to be excreted in the feces Clearance is the sum of all routes of elimination for a particular drug and describes the efficiency of drug removal by the body The correct answer is D. Drugs excreted in the bile enter the intestines where they have 1 of 2 fates. The drug can be excreted in the feces. It may also be processed by intestinal bacteria (usually resulting in the drug being deconjugated) and the resulting free drug can re-enter the systemic circu

Which of the following statements regarding the half-life of a drug is false? When the volume in which a drug distributes increases, so does its half-life The half-life of a drug serves as a measure of the duration of the drug’s action Most drugs are cleared within 3-5 half-lives if no additional doses are administered The half-life of a drug can be increased by administering additional doses When the rate of clearance of a drug decreases, its half-life increases The correct answer is D. The half-life of a drug is independent of the dose size and frequency.

The therapeutic window of Drug Y is narrow. Which of the following statements is true? It would be safer to administer Drug Y in one large daily dose rather than multiple smaller doses throughout the day. Administer the starting dose (ED50) of Drug Y, then monitor symptoms and administer additional Drug Y as needed When the correct dose of Drug Y is administered, the peak plasma concentration of Drug Y will approach the minimal therapeutic concentration Toxicity in Drug Y is rare and generally does not require close monitoring Proper titration of Drug Y is an effective method of preventing overdose The correct answer is E. Titrating drugs with small therapeutic windows is a safe way to prevent the dose from exceeding the minimal toxic concentration.

Which of the following statements regarding drug interactions is false? A drug-drug interaction between Drug J and Drug K can decrease the absorption – and in turn, the bioavailability – of either drug Drug interactions that increase the therapeutic effect of a drug can be used in beneficial ways If Drug F and Drug G affect the same molecular pathway, using both may cause an increased therapeutic effect A drug-drug interaction that promotes renal excretion of a drug will increase that drug’s clearance, which improves its effectiveness Drugs can interact at both the receptor or system level The correct answer is D. If a drug-drug interaction promotes renal excretion of a drug, it will increase that drug’s clearance and reduce its effectiveness

Which of the following statements regarding drug use is false? A contraindication for a drug suggests that the drug is harmful and should not be used in a particular patient Monitoring for improvement or worsening symptoms following drug prescription is a part of the World Health Organization’s 6 steps of rational prescription A patient’s disease state is unlikely to interact with any drugs they may be taking and does not require any follow up Patients should be made aware of any foods they should avoid when given a new prescription to prevent drug-food interactions An example of a preventable adverse event would be where a patient was administered Drug Z instead of Drug A because the bottle for Drug Z had been accidentally misplaced where Drug A is typically found on the shelf The correct answer is C. Drug-disease interactions are less well-characterized than drug-drug and drug-food interactions, but it is known that they occur. For example, influenza can alter drug metabolism and lead to toxicity.

Which pharmacokinetic parameters is LEAST affected by differences in sex: Absorption Distribution Metabolism Excretion The correct answer is C. Sex differences in metabolism are subtle and may be clinically relevant for only a few drugs.

Which of the following statements are FALSE: Women are at 2x greater risk of adverse drug events than men Early-stage liver disease is a major determinant of drug response Most people carry at least one genetic variation that impacts drug effectiveness Drugs with a narrow therapeutic window are more likely to be affected by drugdrug interactions The correct answer is B. The liver has significant functional reserves, so only severe disease will cause noticeable effects on organ function.

Why might it not be appropriate to extrapolate the dosing of an adult oral medication into children: Children have lower stomach acid production, leading to changes in drug absorption Children have a larger surface area to volume ratio, leading to differences in systemic drug exposure Children have lower gut transit speeds, leading to differences in drug processing times Children often have multi-morbidities, increasing the risk of drug-drug interaction effects The correct answer is A. Body surface area to volume ratio affects topically applied medicines, children have faster gut transit speeds, and children do not often have multiple simultaneous conditions leading polypharmacy considerations.

Which populations may present with decreased glomerular filtration rates: i) 6 month olds ii) 76 year olds iii) Females iv) 3 year olds v) African descent i, ii, iv i, ii iii, v i, ii, v The correct answer is B. Children have decreased kidney function, reaching adult rates only at around 1 year old. Kidney function of children 3-6 year old exceeds the activity of normal adults. Old age is also associated with decreased GFR. There is no indication that sex or race influences GFR.

What is the STEPS program: Approach to breaking bad news to patients Screening tool for evaluating non-alcohol-related substance abuse List of considerations for minimizing risk of adverse drug events National initiative to encourage more physical activity in the elderly population The correct answer is C. STEPS stands for Safety, tolerability, effectiveness, price, and simplicity.

Which of the following is NOT a barrier to deprescribing: Lack of knowledge surrounding the medication’s effect Prevailing medical culture promotes increased medication use Pharmacists earn a percentage for each prescription filled Patient is reluctant to stop taking certain medications The correct answer is C. Lack of knowledge, medical culture, and patient preferences are all barriers to deprescribing. Pharmacists in Canada are not paid per prescription, and will often advocate for and help identify opportunities for deprescribing.

Which of the following is the correct description of a drug development stage: Phase IV – Comparison to other countries Preclinical – First in humans Phase III – Comparison to the standard of care Phase I – Animal studies The correct answer is C. Preclinical is in animals; Phase I is first in humans; Phase II is first in patients; Phase III is comparison to the standard of care; Phase IV is post-marketing surveillance.

What is a provincial Formulary: A list of drugs covered under the province’s drug plan A list of drugs approved for use in the province’s health system The province’s process for drug approval Both A and B The correct answer is D. The provincial Formulary stipulates the list of drugs approved for use and those that are covered under the province’s drug plan. Drug approval is governed at the Federal level, under Health Canada.

The patient’s ECF osmolarity is decreased The patient’s ICF volume is increased The patient’s plasma level of ANP is decreased The patient’s plasma level of ADH is decreased The correct answer is C. Patient’s ANP in response to fluid overload should increase and not decrease,

Fibrous Scarring Hyperplasia Hypertrophy Regeneration The correct answer is C. Existing heart muscles will hypertrophy in response to an increased workload

Fibrous Scarring Hyperplasia Hypertrophy Regeneration The correct answer is A. Heart can only repair damage through scarring Explanation for above questions:. Heart can only repair damage through scarring while the majority of tissue could do regeneration repair.

A patient is in an accident which causes a lesion in her spinal cord. Which of the following symptoms is typical for someone who has a spinal cord injury? No significant atrophy Tendon reflexes reduced or absent Normal tone No fasciculations A & D The correct answer is E. This is an upper motor neuron injury so there shouldn’t be any significant atrophy or fasciculations

Which of the following does NOT affect someone’s medical fitness to drive? Hearing Drugs Fluctuating conditions Neuromuscular conditions Cognition The correct answer is A. The rest of the choices are from the CAN DRIVE pneumonic. It is vision not hearing that affects medical fitness to drive.

Which of the following is a criterion for duty to warn/report? Concern for imminent severe bodily harm Adult patient seeking care for domestic abuse Unlikable patient Adult patient who has experienced sexual assault Patient who seeks help for depression who is not considering suicide The correct answer is A. Which of the following examples follows the principles of choosing wisely: Dr. Scolio, a family practitioner, refers all his patients with lower back pain to be imaged in case they are suffering from osteosarcoma of the spine Dr. Boone, a hematologist, orders two separate rounds of electrolytes for all her consults in the ER to make sure the first lab result was not messed up Dr. Jefe, a family physician, prescribes antibiotics for all her patients that present with cold like symptoms Dr. Jin, an otolaryngologist, orders a urine test as pre-op workup to remove a neck mass in an otherwise healthy patient Dr. Emciel, a sport med doctor that orders x-rays to first image all his patients with knee problems, even though an MRI would allow him to diagnose PCL tears if they were present The correct answer is E. Falls of any kind are a cause for concern for in elderly patients. True False The correct answer is A. In an older adult any fall matters: falls are one of the geriatric syndromes, and a fall can be the only sign of a serious illness such as an MI, an infection or hyperthyroidism.

Hearing impairments are not uncommon for older patients. Which of the following is NOT an appropriate strategy when interviewing patients with hearing impairments? Raise your pitch Speak slightly slower Articulate clearly Face the patient to assist with lip reading If they wear a hearing aid, ensure that it’s working The correct answer is A. For which of the following patients would taking a collateral history be helpful? Mx. S who is 68 years old and has a history of progressive dementia. A collateral history is recommended for pts with communication problems, memory problems, or those with unintentional minimization of difficulties. Be careful not to infantilize seniors; not every senior patient will need a collateral history, even if they’re quite old.

Which of the following scenarios best showcases the concepts of frailty? A patient who is hospitalized after being struck by a car but makes a full recovery A patient who contracts Necrotizing Fasciitis and must have both his limbs amputated making them unable to walk A patient who lives in a nursing home A patient who is in the hospital after catching the cold and now has reduced lung capacity The correct answer is D. Frailty increases one’s vulnerability to adverse outcomes. Frail patients who encounter minor stressors (like a cold) may take a longer period of time to recover and may permanently experience reduced functioning.

Which of the following is a characteristic of pseudodementia (depression)? Chronic, progressive Provides details about cognitive problems when asking about subjective complaints Fluctuating mood Slow, deteriorating course Makes an effort when assessed The correct answer is B. Which four of the following options are reasons/explanations for atypical presentations in elderly patients? Atypical presentations are signs/symptoms that differ from the “classic” or most common presentations of that disease. Lower intelligence, confusion, impatience, poor compliance and early presentations are not explanations of atypical presentations in the elderly.

Which of the drugs shown in the graph is the most potent? Drug A Drug B Drug C Drug B & Drug C are both the most potent The correct answer is A. Potency is the drug concentration (EC50) or drug dosage (ED50) required to produce 50% of the maximal effect/response. Hematopoiesis, Hemoglobin and RBC Morphology Every blood cell comes from one pluripotent stem cell maturing along a fixed sequence in the marrow; knowing that sequence, and what normal RBCs look like, is what lets you read a CBC and a smear. Only bands and segmented granulocytes normally leave the marrow. Leukemia type tracks the maturation arrest: myeloblast = AML, promyelocyte = APL, none = CML . EPO comes from the kidney, TPO from the liver. α-globin: 2 genes on chr 16; β-globin: 1 gene on chr 11; HbF → HbA by 3-6 months. Smear clues: bite cells = G6PD , schistocytes = MAHA , teardrops = myelofibrosis , rouleaux = myeloma . Components of blood Plasma : non-cellular fluid of blood — water, proteins (albumin), coagulation factors, immunoglobulins Serum : the liquid left after blood has clotted (plasma minus coagulation factors and fibrinogen) Spun blood: ~55% plasma, ~1% buffy coat (platelets + WBCs), ~44% RBCs. The CBC and the Coulter Counter The CBC is the starting point of every anemia workup: it counts each cell line and, through the Coulter counter, sizes the red cells. A CBC reports WBC, RBC (Hb, HCT, MCV, RDW) and platelet (count, MPV) values; the differential splits WBCs into five types. The Coulter counter counts cells and derives their size from the electrical pulse each one makes. The complete blood count CBC : venous blood sample analysed for its cellular components White cells : leukocyte count (LKC) Red cells : erythrocyte count (ERC), hemoglobin (Hb), hematocrit (HCT), mean cell volume (MCV), RBC distribution width (RDW) Platelets : platelet (thrombocyte) count, mean platelet volume (MPV) CBC + white cell differential (CBC+diff, CBC/D) adds the breakdown: neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, basophils A sample CBC/D report: every value is read against its reference range (here low WBC, Hb and platelets with a normal MCV — a pancytopenia). The Coulter counter Laboratory instrument that counts blood cells and measures their indices Cells in a conductive liquid are drawn through a small aperture between two electrodes; each cell briefly changes the electrical signal, and the size of the pulse reflects the size of the cell Each cell passing the aperture produces one voltage pulse; a large cell gives a taller pulse (C) than a small cell (D).

Microcytic Anemia (MCV < 80 fL) Microcytosis means hemoglobin synthesis has fallen behind cell division — from too little iron, iron that cannot be used, or too little globin. TAILS names the causes. TAILS . Iron deficiency: find the source of loss, ↑ RDW and transferrin. Chronic inflammation: hepcidin blocks ferroportin — functional deficiency with ↑ ferritin. Sideroblastic: iron in mitochondria, B6 deficiency , Pappenheimer bodies. Thalassemia is quantitative: β-thal minor ↑ HbA2, major ↑ HbF ; α-thal has normal HbA2. Mechanism Erythrocyte-precursor nuclei divide at a regular pace that outruns Hb synthesis → extra divisions → small, pale RBCs Differential — TAILS : T halassemia, A nemia of chronic inflammation, I ron deficiency, L ead poisoning, S ideroblastic anemia The four main microcytic anemias (lead poisoning appears under sideroblastic). non-GI: menstruation, fibroids, urinary loss, chronic intravascular hemolysis with hemoglobinuria, pulmonary hemosiderosis, bleeding disorder, marathon running, blood donation Iron depletion = deficiency without anemia Acute/chronic immune activation Chronic infection : lung abscess, TB, subacute bacterial endocarditis, osteomyelitis, HIV Chronic inflammation : RA, SLE, rheumatic fever, IBD Malignancy : lymphoma, carcinoma, myeloma Alcoholic liver disease, heart disease Idiopathic Hepcidin overproduction blocks ferroportin from releasing stored iron → functional iron deficiency Iron deposits in mitochondria ( ring around the precursor nucleus ) Congenital : X-linked, autosomal recessive Acquired : toxins, vitamin B6 deficiency , myelodysplastic syndromes Iron present in normal amounts but cannot enter Hb ( functional iron deficiency ) α- or β-globin gene defects ( quantitative ); Normocytic Anemia (MCV 80-100 fL) A normal-sized red cell with too few of them means the marrow is losing, failing, suppressed or being outpaced by destruction — ABCD. ABCD : acute blood loss, bone marrow failure, chronic disease, destruction. PRCA = severe reticulocytopenia ; aplastic = pancytopenia with fatty marrow ; myelophthisis = leukoerythroblastic film with teardrops . Sickle cell: Glu → Val , hidden by HbF until ~3, penicillin prophylaxis to age 5 , hydroxyurea. Differential — ABCD A cute blood loss B one marrow failure — pure red cell aplasia, aplastic anemia, myelophthisis C hronic disease (anemia of chronic inflammation — see microcytic anemia) D estruction — hemolysis (see hemolytic anemia), including sickle cell disease Bone marrow failure — one line (PRCA), all lines (aplastic), or marrow crowded out (myelophthisis). Macrocytic Anemia (MCV > 97 fL) Big red cells come either from impaired DNA synthesis (B12/folate — megaloblastic) or from membrane and counting effects (liver, reticulocytes, clumping, thyroid). ABCDEF names them. B12 stores last 3-4 years, folate 3-6 months. B12 deficiency ↑ methylmalonic acid + homocysteine; folate ↑ homocysteine only — and only B12 gives neurologic signs (proprioception, neuropathy). Megaloblastic film: oval macrocytes + hypersegmented neutrophils ; liver disease gives round macrocytes with normal neutrophils. Myeloma and cold agglutinins cause pseudo-macrocytosis . Differential — ABCDEF A lcoholism (liver disease) B 12 deficiency C ompensatory reticulocytosis D rugs / dysplasia E ndocrine (hypothyroidism) F olate deficiency / f etus (pregnancy) Megaloblastic causes — the metabolites separate them. Approach to Hemolytic Anemia Hemolysis leaves the same chemical fingerprint whatever the cause; the DAT and the smear then split immune from intrinsic red-cell defects. Hemolysis = ↑ indirect bilirubin, ↑ LDH, ↑ retics, ↓ haptoglobin . DAT+ IgG = warm (37°C) ; DAT+ C3 = cold (IgM, Mycoplasma/mono) . DAT− with bite cells/Heinz bodies = G6PD (fava, sulfa, antimalarials); with spherocytes = HS (band 3 flow). Mechanical valves and MAHA give schistocytes ; PNH is PIGA, not immune. Oral iron: retics in 1 week, stores in 3-6 months. Myelodysplastic Syndromes and Iron, Folate and B12 Metabolism MDS is a clonal marrow failure that makes cells badly and can become AML; the second half covers how the marrow's raw materials — iron, folate and B12 — are absorbed, stored and used. MDS : elderly (median 65-70), cytopenias, AML risk , staged by IPSS ; higher risk → hypomethylating agents; del(5q) → lenalidomide . Hepcidin blocks ferroportin. Ferritin = stores; chelate if > 1000. B12: IF in duodenum, absorbed in ileum, stores 3-5 years ; folate stores 3-4 months. B12 serves both methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase — folate only the first. Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) Group of clonal hematopoietic stem cell malignancies : ineffective hematopoiesis in ≥ 1 lineage, peripheral cytopenias, and risk of transformation to AML 3-4 per 100,000; far more common in the elderly (1 in 1000); median age 65-70 Etiology : idiopathic, or secondary to toxins (chemotherapy, radiation, environmental); may accompany a hereditary disorder or acquired mutations Presentation : anemia (80% at diagnosis, normocytic or macrocytic), neutropenia (40%), thrombocytopenia (30%), progression to AML Ix : CBC (cytopenias), ferritin (iron overload), BM aspirate/biopsy, flow cytometry, cytogenetics IPSS (International Prognostic Scoring System): BM blast %, chromosomal abnormalities, number of cell lines involved MDS with del(5q) : < 10% of MDS → macrocytic anemia + thrombocytosis ; Approach to a Bleeding Patient and Transfusion Stabilize first, stop the bleeding, then work out the cause. The history — mucosal vs deep bleeding — points to platelets/vWF versus coagulation factors before any lab result, and transfusion replaces only the component that is missing. Mucosal = primary hemostasis (platelets, vWD); joints/muscle = secondary (hemophilia). Normal PT/aPTT does not exclude bleeding (vWD, platelets, FXIII ). Hemophilia: X-linked, aPTT ↑ PT normal . vWD type 1 → DDAVP . Transfuse RBCs at Hb < 70 , platelets at < 10 (50 surgery, 100 neurosurgery); no platelets in TTP/HUS/HIT . O− universal RBC donor, AB universal plasma donor. PCC for warfarin reversal — plus IV vitamin K . The three steps Stabilize the patient — ABCs : airway open and protected, breathing, circulation (blood volume) Deal with the bleeding — identify the cause, stop it, and maintain adequate levels of each blood component Work up the cause — history, exam, differential, investigations History — the most important tool Sets the pre-test probability of a bleeding disorder and separates congenital from acquired causes. Onset : spontaneous, or with hemostatic challenges (dental extraction, surgery, postpartum, vaccination) Location : mucosal → more likely primary ; internal/deep → more likely secondary hemostasis defect Pattern : bruises, petechiae, hematomas;
