These chemicals inhibit passive sodium reabsorption by principal cells in the collecting duct Thiazide diuretics Loop diuretics K-sparing diuretics Prostaglandins The correct answer is C. Which of the following best illustrates the mechanism by which ADH functions? It allows cells of the thick ascending loop of Henle to form aquaporins so water can flow into the filtrate It increases the activity of transport pumps in the descending loop of Henle so more water can be absorbed It allows cells of the collecting ducts to form aquaporins so water can flow into the interstitium It decreases the activity of transport pumps in the distal convoluted tubule so less solute is absorbed The correct answer is C. ADH primarily leads to the formation of aquaporins (water channels) in the collecting ducts so water can flow out of the filtrate into the interstitum. ADH also increases the activity of transporters in the thick ascending limb.

Which of the following physiological changes would NOT be expected in a patient who develops hypernatremia? Brain cells begin to shrink Increased thirst Decreased levels of ADH Decreased levels of aldosterone The correct answer is C. Patients with hypernatremia have too little water. As a result of being in a hypertonic solution, brain cells lose water by osmosis and shrink. Hyperosmolarity of the blood leads to increased secretion of ADH, leading to increased thirst. Christopher is a marathon runner. During one of his marathons on a hot July day, he was sweating heavily and replenishing with water on road-side tables at every 2-km mark. After the race, he drank another one liter of water. He started feeling confused and weak due to critical hyponatremia. What physiological response was happening in this situation? Chris’s glomerular filtration rate decreased Chris’s brain cells were shrinking due to a hypotonic extracellular fluid Chris’s adrenal glands were secreting less aldosterone Chris’s hypothalamus was not secreting ADH The correct answer is D. By consuming too much free water, Christopher’s blood would become hyponatremic. Christopher’s kidneys would compensate by creating dilute urine. Which of the following options would suggest a diagnosis of nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus in a patient with hypernatremia and a high urine volume? low urine osmolality that responds to exogenous ADH (urine becomes more concentrated) low urine osmolality that does not respond to exogenous ADH high urine osmolality with low sodium and potassium concentrations high urine osmolality with high sodium and potassium concentrations The correct answer is B. Diabetic Insipidus is characterized by high volume urine that is very dilute. In Type 2 diabetes, the pancreas properly synthesizes insulin; however, cells do not respond to it, leading to elevated serum glucose levels. Manfred is presenting to his family doctor for the first time with symptoms of Type 2 diabetes. Which of the following blood test results or physical examination results are expected? Manfred’s urine osmolarity is low. Manfred’s urine volume is low. Manfred’s urine is high in sodium and potassium. Manfred has high blood plasma sodium concentrations. The correct answer is D. In Type 2 diabetes, the increased sugar in the blood allows for osmotic diuresis in the urine, leading to increased urine production with high urine osmolarity. What are two potential causes of cerebral edema? Hyponatremia causes the cells in the brain to absorb more water by osmosis, leading to fatal brain swelling. If this is not corrected quickly enough, this can lead to cerebral edema. Mr. Taylor presents to the ER in a distressed and fatigue state. After the patient's vitals are taken and maintained, an arterial blood gas is taken which reveals the patient has metabolic acidosis . Which of the following pathologies is the patient likely NOT suffering from? pH: 7.25 HCO3-: 12 Anion gap: 20 Methanol poisoning Osmotic diarrhea Lactic acidosis Diabetic ketoacidosis Iron poisoning The correct answer is B. The patient is suffering from metabolic acidosis (drop in bicarbonate levels). The patient also has a large anion gap, which can indicate that other organic acids are accumulating as bicarbonate levels are decreasing. The acronym MUDPILES can be used to find a cause for AGMA

The case. Mr. Taylor presents to the ER in a distressed and fatigue state. After the patient's vitals are taken and maintained, an arterial blood gas is taken which reveals the patient has metabolic acidosis . ABG values are displayed below. pH: 7.25 HCO3-: 12 Anion gap: 20 In the previous question, Mr. Taylor’s PCO2 was intentionally not given. If he was mounting an appropriate respiratory response to his metabolic acidosis, what should his CO2 levels be? 52 mmHg 28 mmHg 46 mmHg 34 mmHg The correct answer is B. If the patient had mounted an appropriate respiratory response by breathing more (to expel more CO2) there would be an equivalent reduction in CO2 as there was in HCO3- (1:1 ratio). Since Bicarbonate decreased by 12, CO2 should have also decreased by 12 (and 40 – 12 = 28).

The anion gap is calculated by: [Na+] - [Cl- + HCO3-]. Given the patient’s blood results, the anion gap is [136 - (110+14)] = 12. With a normal albumin level of 40 g/L, this anion gap is normal.

Which of the following is a potential cause of anion-gap metabolic acidosis? Diabetic ketoacidosis Salicylate poisoning Ethylene glycol poisoning A and B A, B, and C The correct answer is E. All of these are part of the MUDPILES acronym for possible causes of anion-gap metabolic acidosis.

A patient presents to the ER in a state of distress. An ECG displays long slender T waves and a slightly stretched out QRS complex. A patient presents with hypokalemia. In addition to this they have a high TTKG (11) and on physical exam they have extensive pitting edema up to the level of their kneecap. Which of the following options best explain the patient’s presentation? Overuse of aldosterone antagonists Overuse of diuretics Overproduction of aldosterone Decreased intake of potassium The correct answer is C. Excessive aldosterone secretion leads to increased reabsorption of sodium, which can manifest as pitting edema and fluid build-up throughout the body. Bill is 67 years old, and his wife brought him to the emergency room after a fall resulting in pain and bruising at his hip. An X-ray revealed a hip fracture. Which of the following fluids should be considered for a hypovolemic patient? Select all that apply. 5% Dextrose in water Normal saline Free water Colloid solution BD . The maintenance rate rule-of-thumb for IV fluids follows the 4:2:1 rule. For the first 10 kg, a patient receives 4 mL/kg/hr. For the second 10 kg, a patient receives 2 mL/kg/hr. Anything beyond 20 kg, the patient receives an additional 1 mL/kg/hr. For a 60 kg patient, this a

Which of the following formulas/markers is ideal for measuring glomerular filtration rate? Serum creatinine and Cockcroft-Gault equation Serum creatinine and CKD-EPI formula Blood urea nitrogen and Cockcroft-Gault equation Blood urea nitrogen and CKD-EPI formula The correct answer is B. Serum creatinine levels and the CKD-EPI formula are the best indicators for glomerular filtration rate. Serum Creatinine is a more reliable measure of GFR than BUN because urea can be reabsorbed by the kidney. Serum creatinine is comparatively relatively more stable.

A patient presents with glomerulonephritis. Which of the following findings would you expect to see in their microscopic urinalysis? Red blood cells White blood cells Casts filled with white blood cells Casts filled with red blood cells The correct answer is D. The presence of casts filled with RBCs can be suggestive of glomerulonephritis. The presence of casts filled with WBCs can be suggestive of Interstitial nephritis. White blood cells can be suggestive of a urinary tract infection and RBCs can be suggestive of cancer or kidney

Which statement of the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is true? Elevated BUN levels are pathognomonic for a decrease in renal function. The gold standard for assessing GFR is observing how much insulin is passed by the kidneys Patients with larger muscular build will inherently have larger creatinine levels than patients with smaller muscular build GFR tests involving Cystatin C are accurate for adults but do not provide valid results for children The correct answer is C. Creatinine levels are affected by many things, including muscle mass. Elevated BUN levels could indicate many different pathologies. Option B would be true if the answer said inulin, not insulin. Lastly, Cystatin C is a good test for children, but less valid for adults.

Kenneth is 76 years old with a lifelong history of smoking, excess alcohol consumption, and a high cholesterol diet. In recent years, his kidney function has declined considerably. Recently, he has developed painful urination and hematuria consistent with kidney stones. Which imaging modality should be used to confirm the diagnosis? Ultrasound MRI Renal biopsy CT scan with contrast Intravenous pyelogram The correct answer is A. An ultrasound is a good first test. CT scans with contrast are valuable tests in general, but with Kenneth’s reduced kidney function, the contrast agent could be too dangerous for him.

A 50-year-old patient with suspected heavy metal ingestion (occupation as a steelworker) undergoes a urinalysis, which reveals moderate protein uremia. Glomerular proteinuria Tubular proteinuria Overflow proteinuria Tissue proteinuria Arrange for a kidney biopsy Order an ANA and anti-DNA test No intervention required The correct answer is B, G. The presence of Tamm Horsfall protein (or B2 microglobulin) indicates the patient may have tubular proteinuria. This can result from heavy metal, or any disease that damages the PCT. This is often not associated with any pathological condition – thus no further treatment

The presence of high albumin levels (proteinuria) and the long history of T2D is characteristic of a patient presenting with glomerular proteinuria. What is the likely pathology when a patient presents with hematuria but no proteinuria? This could be glomerular hematuria This could be macroalbuminuria This could be a kidney stone in the ureters This could be natural progression of Type 2 Diabetes The correct answer is C. This suggests a structural issue, such as the presence of an obstruction in the ureters like a kidney stone. Glomerular hematuria is characterized by high urine albumin levels (proteinuria).

Which of the following statements regarding chronic kidney disease is true? To meet the criteria of CKD, patients need kidney damage and an eGFR below 60 ml/min The incidence of CKD is decreasing in the overall population Patients with CKD are contraindicated for ACEi and ARBs It’s not uncommon for older individuals (older than 80) to have a low (<60 mL/min) GFR The correct answer is D. To meet the criteria of CKD patients need kidney damage OR a reduced eGFR below 60 ml/min. The incidence of CKD is increasing as people are living longer lives. Patients with CKD often require ACEi and ARBs to manage their blood pressure and prevent further decline of their

Recommending a low-salt diet Recommending reduced dietary protein consumption Prescribing a statin Prescribing an angiotensin receptor blocker Referral for dialysis The correct answer is E. In chronic kidney disease, the treatments are to control blood pressure (eg, reduce salt in the diet), control hyperlipidemia (eg, prescribe a statin), reduce the GFR (eg, with ACE-i’s or ARBs), and restrict protein consumption in the diet. You are a resident doctor in the emergency room currently overseeing four patients with renal pathologies. A patient with pseudohyperkalemia A patient with blood pH of 7.23, PCO2 of 20 mmHg, and [HCO3-] of 20 mmol/L A patient who has overdosed on salicylates A patient with Stage 4 chronic kidney disease The correct answer is C. Indications for dialysis are metabolic acidosis, electrolyte imbalances, ingestion of drugs or ischemia, overload of fluid, or uremia. The patient in option B has respiratory acidosis. Only the patient in option C satisfies any of these indications for dialysis. Patients wit

The inferior vena cava proceeds into the abdominal cavity via the caval opening located in the central tendon. The abdominal aorta proceeds through the opening made by the left and right crus. The esophageal hiatus is a muscular hiatus where the esophagus passes through. The

An injury to the femoral nerve can lead to a loss of motor innervation to which muscle? Psoas major Psoas minor Iliacus Quadratus Lumborum The correct answer is C. The iliacus is innervated by the femoral nerve. The anterior rami innervates the Psoas major and minor, and the Quadratus Lumborum.

Which option below correctly matches an anatomical structure with its embryological origin? The kidney develops from the mesonephros The adrenal glands develop from the pronephros The ureters develop from the metanephros The renal arteries develop from the hemanephros The correct answer is C. The mesonephros and pronephros serve functions only in the embryo. The renal system is derived from the metanephros. Hemanephros is a made-up term.

In a cardiac catherization, debris is scraped of the wall, the cholesterol crystals can proceed into circulation and occlude small vessels - leading to vascular marking in the patient’s extremities. A 67-year-old patient with a 50% block in his left anterior descending artery went to the interventional cardiology lab for a stent. In this procedure, a catheter is inserted into the radial artery and fed toward the aortic valve. The catheter is threaded into the coronary arteries with the assistance of contrast agent. The management for patients with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) and Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) with nephropathy are slightly different. Which statement(s) below is true? Select all that apply. A patient with T2D is screened for microalbuminuria 5 years after diagnosis; a patient with T1D is screened for microalbuminuria immediately Patients with T2D are prescribed sodium-glucose-co-transport inhibitors (such as dapagliflozin); patients with T1D are not. Reduction of dietary protein is recommended for patients if they are already consuming a large amount of protein. The re

Which of the following medications should not be taken together? Loop diuretics and calcium supplements Loop diuretics and potassium supplements Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists and loop diuretics Potassium-sparing diuretics and potassium supplements The correct answer is D. Use the following answers for the next SEVEN questions. Which diuretic works primarily in the thick ascending limb of the Loop of Henle? Mannitol Furosemide Hydrochlorothiazide Chlorthalidone Spironolactone The correct answer is B. Loop Diuretics work in the thick ascending loop of Henle.

Use the following answers for the next SEVEN questions. Which diuretic is generally the most efficacious? Mannitol Furosemide Hydrochlorothiazide Chlorthalidone Spironolactone The correct answer is B. Loop Diuretics are generally the most efficacious diuretic as they work in the TAL where a large amount of sodium is excreted into the filtrate.

Use the following answers for the next SEVEN questions. Which diuretic can lead to hypercalcemia in a patient? Mannitol Furosemide Hydrochlorothiazide Chlorthalidone Spironolactone The correct answer is C, D. These thiazide-type diuretics lead to increased absorption of calcium, due to increased activity of the Na/Ca antiporter. As more sodium is excreted, more calcium is reabsorbed.

Use the following answers for the next SEVEN questions. Which diuretic is most appropriate for Mr. Anderson, a 40-year-old computer programmer with hypertensive hypokalemia? Mannitol Furosemide Hydrochlorothiazide Chlorthalidone Spironolactone The correct answer is E. Spironolactone is a K-sparing diuretic. Prescribing this to Mr. Anderson would increase his potassium levels and treat his hypertension.

Use the following answers for the next SEVEN questions. Which diuretic is most appropriate for Mrs. Watson, a 67-year-old with kidney stones? Mannitol Furosemide Hydrochlorothiazide Chlorthalidone Spironolactone The correct answer is C, D. Thiazide diuretics are used to treat kidney stones. Both hydrochlorothiazide (short acting) and chlorthalidone (long acting) are appropriate.

Use the following answers for the next SEVEN questions. Which diuretic is readily filtered by the glomerulus but is not readily reabsorbed, leading to the increased movement of water into the lumen by osmosis? Mannitol Furosemide Hydrochlorothiazide Chlorthalidone Spironolactone The correct answer is A. Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic. This means that it is filtered by the glomerulus but is not readily reabsorbed. This draws water into the lumen by osmosis.

Use the following answers for the next SEVEN questions. Which thiazide-like diuretic is more effective in the treatment of heart failure? Mannitol Furosemide Hydrochlorothiazide Chlorthalidone Spironolactone The correct answer is D. Evidence has shown that long-acting thiazide-like diuretics (like chlorthalidone) reduce cardiovascular events and reduce symptoms of heart failure.

Which of the following statements regarding kidney transplantation is true? Deceased-donor kidney transplants have a better prognosis for the recipient than living-donor kidney transplants Current graft survival rate is slightly over 50% Prednisone is the mainstay of immunosuppression used to manage kidney transplants Calcineurin Inhibitors are associated with an increase in skin cancer and can be nephrotoxic The correct answer is D. Living- Donor kidney transplants have a better prognosis than deceased-donor kidney transplants. Current graft survival rates are around 90-95%. Tacrolimus is the main agent used to induced immunosuppression for patients who underwent a kidney transplant.

What is the species of bacteria that is most often implicated in urinary tract infections and what is the most suitable antibiotic treatment for it? Choose TWO answers. Klebsiella Enterococci E. coli Group B Streptococcus Tripmethoprim Meropenem Ampicillin Nitrofurantoin The correct answer is C, H. E. coli is the most common bacteria leading to urinary tract infections. This is often empirically treated with nitrofurantoin (or maybe Septa -TMP/SMX), to which E. coli is typically susceptible.

Which statement on the treatment of UTIs is correct? Geriatric patients with suspected UTI without symptoms should be treated with broadspectrum antibiotics. Medical management is avoided in women with asymptomatic bacteriuria unless they are pregnant. Urine cultures are necessary for all suspected UTI infections. The most common investigation for a UTI is a genitourinary examination. The correct answer is B. Option A is false - geriatric patients are prescribed antibiotics only when there are symptoms of a urinary tract infection. Urine cultures are not usually performed in the management of UTIs, however some indications for culture are if the patient is symptomatic and elderly

Which of the following options is an appropriate management technique for a patient who gets recurrent urinary tract infections (two UTIs within six months)? Prescribe nitrofurantoin without performing a urine culture Encourage the patient to drink more water and request a urine culture Explore dietary options with the patient No further management is required other than providing reassurance The correct answer is B. Patients with recurrent UTI should have a urine culture done. This is in contrast to those who have a simple uncomplicated UTI, where prescribing antibiotics without a urine culture is appropriate. The urine culture should be used to guide further management steps which incl

Which of the following patients should generally be treated for asymptomatic bacteriuria? Male patients Women over the age of 60 Pregnant women Women on oral contraceptives The correct answer is C. Patients are generally not treated for asymptomatic bacteriuria, however the exception for treatment is for pregnant women. Treating pregnant women can greatly decrease the risk for pyelonephritis, which can cause adverse outcomes for the mother and newborn.

Which bones fuse to form the hip bone? Select three answers Femur Tibia Ischium Ileum Ilium Pubis Symphysis Coccyx The correct answer is C, E, F. These bones fuse to form the hip bone. From 01 - Anatomy of the Pelvis. Each hip bone (os coxae) is three fused bones: the ilium, ischium and pubis , which meet at the acetabulum. The two hip bones meet anteriorly at the pubic symphysis and join the sacrum posteriorly;

A male patient has an overactive sympathetic nervous system. What may be a consequence of this? The patient’s kidneys will produce more urine The patient’s penis will more easily become erect The passage of food through the patient’s large intestine will be slowed The patient’s afferent arteriole will be dilated The correct answer is C. An overactive sympathetic nervous system will lead to a fight-or-flight response, increasing blood pressure, reducing GFR (options A and D are false), and slowing digestion (Option C is false). Erections are promoted by parasympathetic activity, not sympathetic activity.

Which is a method employed by the human body by which the testes are kept at a cooler temperature for the development of healthy sperm cells? Select all that apply. Blood enters the testes via the pampiniform plexus to allow for counter-current heat exchange The cremaster muscle relaxes to lower the level of the testes The dartos muscles contract to increase the surface area of the scrotum The prostate enlarges and shrinks to increase blood flow to the pelvic region The correct answer is B. Options A and C are tempting, however, the Pampiniform plexus is how blood leaves the testicles. The Dartos muscles contract to decrease the surface area of the scrotum, leading to thickening of the skin.

Use the following question stem to answer the next TWO questions. A patient presents to the emergency room concerned about pain in his left flank that developed over the past 2 days. Ultrasound reveals a mass obstructing the patient’s left ureter and hydronephrosis of the left kidney. The patient’s right ureter and kidney are normal. Urinalysis reveals a normal creatinine and BUN levels, and no evidence of a UTI. Assume the mass is benign. What is the next step in the patient’s management? Refer to a urologist for official diagnosis Immediate and urgent referral to surgery to fix the obstruction Insertion of a urethral foley catheter to relieve the obstruction Insertion of a ureteral stent within six weeks of the onset of symptoms The correct answer is D. Ureteric obstructions should be treated within six weeks of the onset of symptoms. If a UTI develops, the urgency increases, and immediate treatment is required. Since the obstruction is in the ureters, a Foley catheter would not be helpful - a ureteric stent is needed.

Use the following question stem to answer the next TWO questions. A patient presents to the emergency room concerned about pain in his left flank that developed over the past 2 days. Ultrasound reveals a mass obstructing the patient’s left ureter and hydronephrosis of the left kidney. The patient’s right ureter and kidney are normal. Urinalysis reveals a normal creatinine and BUN levels, and no evidence of a UTI. Assume the mass is benign. Shortly after the ureteric obstruction is relieved, the patient develops lethargy and weakness consistent with hypokalemia. What is the most likely underlying cause of this? Medications post-operation include thiazide-diuretics, which lead to hypokalemia. After the obstruction is relieved, the patient can expel large volumes of urine, leading to hypokalemia. Irreversible kidney damage has led to excess excretion of potassium. Normal creatinine and BUN levels indicate pre-renal failure leading to hypokalemia. The correct answer is B. Relief of a urinary tract obstruction can lead to post-obstructive diuresis, leading to increased urine production and potassium loss. This can lead to hypokalemia. If the obstruction is relieved within six weeks, kidney damage is not likely.

As a physician you’re currently seeing a patient, Taylor (a 35-year-old female) with severe renal colic and an inability to void for the past 12+ hours. Their BUN/creatinine ratio is significantly elevated, and a renal ultrasound reveals bilateral obstruction of the proximal ureters. Which of the following is the NEXT appropriate management step given the findings? Insert a urethral foley catheter Insert a suprapubic catheter Insert a ureteral stent Perform a ureteroscopy to remove stones Pharmacotherapy (alpha-blockers, finasteride) The correct answer is C. The patient is experiencing a urinary tract obstruction likely from a stone occluding the proximal ureter. The most immediate management step involves temporarily relieving the obstruction through a ureteral stent placement. Urethral foley catheter or suprapubic catheter are

The case. As a physician you’re currently seeing a patient, Taylor (a 35-year-old female) with severe renal colic and an inability to void for the past 12+ hours. Their BUN/creatinine ratio is significantly elevated, and a renal ultrasound reveals bilateral obstruction of the proximal ureters. The patient in the previous question (35-year-old Taylor, female), undergoes an appropriate temporary measure and a few days later undergoes an operation to remove the stones occluding her ureters. The patient is discharged from the hospital. Three days later the patient returns to your clinic to report that they’ve been urinating an excessive amount (several liters every day). Which of the following is an appropriate management step, given the patient’s status? Consider prescribing an Angiontensin II/ ARB Order a CT scan to examine for Hydronephrosis Consider ureter stent removal Give reassurance and encourage adequate fluid intake The correct answer is D. Post Obstructive Diuresis is a common occurrence after urinary tract obstruction. This is largely due to disruption in the kidney’s ability to concentrate the urine and is usually a self- resolving process. The physician should reassure the patient and encourage fluid intake

During a regular DRE, a physician notices that his 56-year-old patient has an enlarged prostate. The patient complains of some frequent urination, weak stream, and incomplete emptying upon voiding. Ultrasound tests indicate that the middle lobe of the prostate is enlarged. The patient has been informed of some of the side effects of surgical therapy and instead has chosen a medical management. Which medicine would you prescribe to the patient to shrink the prostate gland? TURP therapy Diuretics Alpha-blocker therapy 5-alpha reductase inhibitors Calcium-channel blockers The correct answer is D. 5-alpha reductase inhibitors shrink the prostate. Alpha-blockers relax the muscles of the prostate and bladder, improving urine flow. TURP is an invasive treatment not indicated for this patient (who doesn’t want a surgical therapy).

A 65-year-old male patient presents to your clinic with concerns of frequent urination, a weak stream and increased straining to urinate. The patient has been experiencing these symptoms for the past month and he feels that it takes a significant toll on his everyday life. A urinalysis and urine culture reveals no significant findings. A digital rectal exam is suggestive of a considerably enlarged prostate. Which of the following is an appropriate management to consider to treat the suspected diagnosis. Choose THREE options. Pelvic floor physiotherapy Dihydrotestosterone Alpha-blockers NSAIDs Broad spectrum antibiotics 5-alpha reductase therapy Transurethral resection of the prostrate The correct answer is C, F, G. The patient is experiencing LUTS (Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms – frequency, urgency, Nocturia, Weak stream, Intermittency, Straining, Incomplete emptying) which is highly suggestive of benign prostatic hyperplasia. The negative urinalysis and urine culture rules out bl

Two years ago, 63-year-old Wallace’s PSA levels were slightly elevated at 7 ng/mL. A prostate biopsy was performed indicating the presence of prostate cancer. This year, Wallace’s PSA levels are 14 ng/mL (with notable prostate enlargement since his last physical examination). Wallace is requesting therapy. Which statement below is true? Prostate cancer has a good prognosis even if metastasis has occurred For many patients, the risks of treating prostate cancer outweigh the benefits Brachytherapy involves surgically shining high-intensity radio-waves on the affected area TURP is a common treatment choice for prostate cancer The correct answer is B. Prostate screening in Canada is controversial because even with a positive diagnosis, prostate cancer does not often change life expectancy. Many prostate cancer treatments have side effects that a patient is not willing to risk. A comprehensive discussion should be had with

The effectiveness of prostate cancer screening is debated by urologists worldwide. Which statement below is correct? Elevated PSA tests are highly specific for prostate cancer The NNT (number needed to treat) to avoid death by prostate cancer with PSA screening is about 1000 Elevated PSA screening tests leading to a positive diagnosis of prostate cancer require surgical management PSA screening tests are offered for patients ages 40-79 The correct answer is B. For every 1000 patients who undergo a prostate-specific-antigen screening test, 1 person avoids death by prostate cancer [more accurately, 1.28 people in 1000, or an NNT of 732]. Elevated PSA tests are not specific for prostate cancer but could indicate many other benign cau

Which of the following patients should NOT be considered for a serum PSA screening test? A 60-year-old male patient presenting for a routine check-up A 75-year-old male patient presenting for a routine check-up A 55-year-old male patient who recently had surgical resection of their prostate due to prostate cancer A 50-year-old male patient who received a digital rectal exam with a reported palpable nodule The correct answer is B. Serum PSA screening should not be offered to males over the age of 70 – their risk of prostate cancer developing to become a limiting illness is very low. Serum PSA should generally be considered for patients above 50 years old and this can involve a discussion between the d

Which of the following treatments is generally NOT appropriate for early stage prostate cancer? Radical prostatectomy Chemotherapy Brachytherapy External beam radiation The correct answer is B. Radical prostatectomy, brachytherapy and external beam radiation are generally appropriate for patients with early stage prostate cancer. Radical Prostatectomy can also be considered for late stage prostate cancer. Chemotherapy is generally not a part of the treatment for ea

Billy-Ray was getting an abdominal ultrasound to assess for kidney stones when his physician incidentally found a fluid-filled cyst on Billy-Ray’s right kidney. What is the next step in Billy-Ray’s management in dealing with the cyst? Refer to urologist Consider obtaining creatinine and BUN levels with a urinalysis Refer to radiology for a CT scan of the mass Perform a biopsy to assess staging No further tests or management is needed The correct answer is E. Fluid filled cysts are very common and benign. No further tests are needed.

What is the goal for management of advanced kidney cancers? To cure the cancer To improve the patient’s quality of life To prevent further progression To regress the tumour to a more manageable size The correct answer is B. Advanced kidney cancers typically are not curable. Treatment is palliative, aiming to improve the quality of life for patients.

Which tests is a physician likely to order for a 56-year-old patient if an ultrasound reveals a 3-cm mass on a left kidney and a follow-up CT suggests that the mass is neoplastic? Urinalysis Urine culture Urine dipstick CT of the abdomen/pelvis Chest X-ray Genetic analysis Liver enzymes Kidney biopsy The correct answer is D, E, G. These tests are to stage the cancer (CT of the abdomen and pelvis) and rule out metastasis of the kidney cancer, which occurs most often in the lungs (Chest X-ray / CT of the chest), liver (liver enzymes), lymph nodes (CT of abdomen and pelvis), bone (not listed, but s

A 50-year-old male patient undergoes an initial abdominal ultrasound which reveals a unilateral renal mass. Further follow-up with a CT scan shows a large (12 cm) solid enhancing tumor extending from the body of the kidney and involving the renal vasculature. The patient is asymptomatic. Further X-rays reveal no metastasis. Which of the following treatment options is mostly appropriate for this current patient? Laparascopic partial nephrectomy Cryoablation Microwave thermal ablation Radical nephrectomy Partial radiation The correct answer is D. A radical nephrectomy is most appropriate as this renal tumour is large and involves the surrounding vasculature. Partial nephrectomy or ablation methods are not appropriate for larger tumours with vascular involvement. Palliative radiation is generally reserved for advanced

Which of the following characteristics of a renal mass on an investigative test (imaging or biopsy) would generally prompt for further investigation/treatment? Choose as many as applicable. A renal mass with internal strictures on ultrasound Dromendary humps noted on renal ultrasound A renal biopsy confirming papillary renal cell carcinoma Type 2 A renal mass delineated with a round, smooth, regular borders on ultrasound A renal mass with enhancement in the corticomedullary phase of the CT scan The correct answer is A, C, E. A renal mass with internal structures is indicative of a complex cyst which can be malignant (low potential). Dromendary humps are not pathological, they are a variation of normal renal anatomy. A patient with cancer affecting his left ureter wants a surgical removal of the tumour. How will the surgeon proceed? The surgeon will remove the ureter and the kidney even if the kidney is not affected The surgery will remove the ureter and the kidney only if the kidney is also affected The surgeon will neither remove the ureter nor the kidney The surgeon will remove both ureters and both kidneys The correct answer is A. Due to the field effect, both the kidney and ureter are removed, even if the kidney is not affected.

What item is not on your differential diagnosis for a patient presenting with hematuria? Benign prostatic hyperplasia Urinary tract infections Kidney stones Lower urinary tract tumour Testicular torsion The correct answer is E. BPH, UTIs, Kidney stones, and lower urinary tract tumours can all present with hematuria, and this is an indication to refer to a urologist for further testing. Testicular torsion is acute and presents with a painful swelling of the testicle. This affects the reproductive sy

A 55-year-old male patient presents to your clinic with concerns of peeing out blood. The patient has worked at a plastic manufacturing plant for the past 20+ years. In addition to hematuria the patient also reports peeing out “stringy clots”. The patient reports no pain when urinating. Which of the following statements is most likely true? The patient’s presentation is in line with an upper urinary tract tumour and this may likely require surgical removal of the ureter and kidney The patient’s presentation is in line with an upper urinary tract tumour and this may likely require surgical removal of solely the ureter The patient’s presentation is in line with a lower urinary tract tumour and this may likely require surgical removal of the urethra and bladder The patient’s presentation is in line with a lower urinary tract tumour and this may likely require surgical removal of solely the bladder The correct answer is A. The presence of stringy clots in the urine suggest the source of bleeding comes from the ureter – and when considering the patient’s extensive work history in a plastics history this can make an upper urinary tract tumour a likely diagnosis. A 60-year-old asymptomatic male patient was recently investigated for microscopic hematuria after taking a urinalysis for an unrelated reason. Investigations revealed this patient had a mild, low grade, superficial urothelial bladder cancer. This finding did not require treatment but the patient had to be screened periodically to check for the progression of this disease. Which of the following investigations is most likely used to assess this? Urinalysis Cystoscopy Renal ultrasound CT abdomen The correct answer is B. Periodic monitoring is done via cystoscopy – an invasive procedure where the physician can examine the lining of your bladder.

Which imaging modality is most commonly used when a patient presents with a scrotal mass? Pelvic X-ray CT Scan Ultrasound MRI Transillumination The correct answer is C. With any scrotal mass, an ultrasound is usually indicated. In many cases, a scrotal ultrasound can lead to the diagnosis of the mass. Transillumination is valuable if suspicious for hydrocele, but not too valuable otherwise. The other imaging modalities become more important

Which of the following statements is true concerning testicular cancer? 10% of all presentations of testicular cancer already involve metastasis Testicular cancer is very curable if metastasis has not occurred, but not curable otherwise Testicular cancer can lead to varicocele or hydrocele Testicular cancer can be staged with an ultrasound The correct answer is A. The initial presentation of testicular cancer involves metastasis in 10-15% of cases. Common sites of metastasis include the abdomen, the chest, the liver, and the brain.

A 13-year-old boy presents to the ER with severe scrotal pain that began one hour ago. The physician performs a localized physical exam of the testes and notices it’s very firm upon palpation. The physician orders an ultrasound which confirms the physician’s suspected diagnosis. Which of the following is likely true regarding this case? The suspected diagnosis was testicular torsion and was confirmed by the presence of arterial blood flow to the affected testicle The suspected diagnosis was testicular torsion and was confirmed by a lack of arterial blood flow to the affected testicle The suspected diagnosis was epididymitis and was confirmed by the presence of arterial blood flow to the affected testicle The suspected diagnosis was epididymitis and was confirmed by the absence of arterial blood flow to the affected testicle The correct answer is B. Testicular torsion often occurs in young males (adolescents) and is accompanied by a sudden onset of pain. The affected testicle are often hard when palpating. Patients with epididymitis are generally older, have a gradual onset of pain, and the testes may tender when palpat

A 65-year-old patient presented to his family physician after he noticed his scrotum is enlarged. A physical exam is conducted, where the physician asks the patient to stand up – there was no enlargement of veins observed (unilaterally or bilaterally). On palpation the physician noted the scrotum was tense but was able to palpate the two testicles. The physician was also able to “get above the mass” (they could feel the mass tapering, and the scrotum was illuminated on transillumination. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? Hernia Varicocele Hydrocele Spermatocele The correct answer is C. Hydrocele is when there is fluid build-up inside the scrotum, which often fives it a tense appearance. To conclusively differentiate a hydrocele from a hernia, a hydrocele can be felt tapering off, whereas the hernia cannot be. Alternatively, the patient can also be asked to

Juan is 12 years old and has a blood pressure that is 127/83 mmHg. For his age and height, a 95th percentile for blood pressure is 123/81 mmHg. Maria is 11 years old and has a blood pressure that is 131/85 mmHg. For her age and height, a 95th percentile for blood pressure is 119/78 mmHg. Both Juan and Maria are asymptomatic and secondary etiologies of hypertension have been ruled out. Select ALL the correct statements. Juan has Stage 1 hypertension and Maria has Stage 2 hypertension. Both Juan and Maria should be assessed for white coat hypertension with ambulatory BP monitoring. Maria requires rapid correction of her blood pressure to the 90th percentile with oral or IV medications. Juan should be prescribed a CCB, an ACE-I, and diuretics immediately. Both Juan and Maria require IV medications. The correct answer is A, C. According to 2017 guidelines, Stage 1 hypertension is defined as >95th percentile, and stage 2 hypertension is defined as 95th percentile + 12 mmHg. Question 545. Erica is an 8-year-old patient who was brought into a pediatric urgent care clinic. In the past 24 hours, Erica has developed acute shortness of breath, fatigue, and confusion. Upon examination, Erica appears unwell, with elevated BP, pitting edema, and minimal urine output. Urinalysis indicates low urine osmolarity and high urine sodium and no evidence of E. coli infection. What is the most likely diagnosis and best treatment option for Erica? Choose TWO answers. Pre-renal AKI Renal AKI Post-renal AKI Treat with IV fluids Treat with fluid restriction Treat with dialysis The correct answer is B, E. The large volume status, low urine osmolarity, and high urine sodium indicate a renal cause of acute kidney injury. The management for this would be fluid restriction. Isaiah is a 5-year-old child with symptoms indicating an acute kidney injury. There is swelling in his legs bilaterally. Perform an ultrasound of Isaiah’s kidneys Perform a biopsy of Isaiah’s kidneys Prescribe prednisone Perform a nephrectomy Watch and wait The correct answer is C. Massive proteinuria indicates a nephrotic syndrome. The most common nephrotic syndrome is minimal change syndrome, followed by focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. The treatment for both of these is prednisone (a steroid). Biopsy is indicated if Isaiah was less than 1 years o

Jeremy is a 6-year-old child with symptoms indicating an acute kidney injury. Yesterday, Jeremy had repeated trips to the bathroom, and today he is edematous. Which statement below is TRUE? Jeremy should be referred for a kidney biopsy to rule out C3 glomerulopathy Jeremy should be started on steroids and immunosuppressants Jeremy should receive supportive treatment and have C3 levels reassessed in 6 weeks Jeremy should toughen up and learn to deal with the pain while he is young Jeremy should receive treatment to boost IgA levels The correct answer is C. Hematuria with mild proteinuria indicates nephritic syndrome. In cases of nephritic syndrome, complement C3 levels are measured. If normal, it indicates IgA nephropathy. If low, it could indicate post-strep glomerulonephritis or C3 glomerulopathy. To assess between these two

A 15-year-old boy is diagnosed with Stage 2 Hypertension after an ambulatory blood pressure was measured to be 145/95 mmHg. The patient presents asymptomatically. Which of the following is an appropriate NEXT step? Repeat blood pressure measurements 1 week later to account for Consider pharmacological treatment with oral Minoxidil Consider non-pharmacological management (diet modification, exercise, salt restriction) Perform investigation to rule-out underlying cause for hypertension The correct answer is B. The patient’s diagnosis of hypertension is accurate as ABP is used and is the goldstandard; white-coat hypertension does not apply to ABP monitoring. Which of the following statements are true regarding nephrotic syndrome and nephritic syndrome? Which of the following findings for a patient being investigated for hemolytic uremic syndrome is suggestive for this disease over a pre-renal injury or renal injury? Oliguria Fluid congestion Thrombocytopenia Hypovolemia High urine osmolality The correct answer is C. Acute Kidney Injury broadly can be characterized by oliguria. Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome is caused by E. coli

What is an indication for an ultrasound when a 12-month-old male presents with undescended testis (UDT)? Perform an ultrasound if the UTD is unilateral and the testis is palpable Perform an ultrasound if the UTD is unilateral and the testes is not palpable Perform an ultrasound if the UTD is bilateral the testes are palpable Perform an ultrasound if the UTD is bilateral the testes are not palpable The correct answer is D. An ultrasound for undescended testicles is rarely useful. However, it is important to perform an ultrasound in cases of bilateral non-palpable testes to assess if the phenotypically male patient is a chromosomally female patient with congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

Which statement below is correct concerning acute scrotal pain in the pediatric population? A patient with testicular torsion should undergo manual detorsion as a first line of therapy. In cases of testicular torsion, the patient should be referred to an emergency urologist immediately. You are seeing a 5-year-old female, Ivy, who has exclusive nighttime enuresis, but voids frequently (12 times) during the day. Her void diary was completed, indicating a functional bladder capacity of 150 mL. When you talk to her, she seems embarrassed and ashamed about her bedwetting, but otherwise seems happy and content. She is doing well in school. Which treatment below would NOT be helpful for Ivy? Recommend that Ivy and her parents set alarms during the night to establish a nighttime routine Reassure Ivy and her parents that most cases of nighttime bedwetting self-resolve with time Suggest consuming less fluids close to bedtime Prescribe oxybutynin, an anti-cholinergic drug to help manage her symptoms Ascertain the cause with an MRI of the bladder The correct answer is E. Ivy’s functional bladder capacity is low (normal bladder capacity = (age+2)*30), which can result in nighttime enuresis. Ivy and her parents should be reassured that this will likely self- resolve. MRIs are indicated only if there is a high suspicion for neurogenic issue.

Verne is 4 years old. His mother brought him into the emergency room because of Verne peeing blood. He also has a fever and left flank pain. Urinalysis tests positive for Enterococci. When vesicoureteral reflux presents with febrile UTIs, a voiding cystourethrogram is indicated to assess for bladder outlines, to grade the VUR, to assess for issues with the urethra, and to assess post-void residual volume. A 8-month-old male is brought into a urologist’s office because his parents are concerned about his testicles. The urologist examines the patient’s scrotum and palpates only one testicle. The urologist can palpate the undescended testicle and bring it down into the scrotum using a physical maneuver, however the testes do not remain there and return to the inguinal region. Which of the following options is an appropriate management step? Instruct the family to bring the patient back at 12 months of age, as the testes can spontaneously descend from 6-12 months of age. The patient has retractile testis – no immediate action needed besides active surveillance Consider performing an inguinal orchidopexy Consider performing a laparascopic examination Consider further investigation with an ultrasound The correct answer is C. This patient has undescended testis. If the patient had retractile testis upon a physical maneuver the patient’s testicle would remain in the scrotum without returning to its original place. Which of the following is a distinguishing marker between physiological and pathological phimosis? Inability to retract the foreskin Pin-point opening Scarring of the foreskin Redness of the foreskin The correct answer is C. Scarring of the foreskin particularly around the opening is suggestive of pathological phimosis. A 35-year-old patient comes to your clinic with concerns of incontinence. She describes that she often experiences involuntary voiding at work when lifting heavy objects or laughing at someone’s joke. Which of the following are appropriate treatments to consider for the presumed diagnosis? Select TWO Answers. Pelvic floor exercises Midurethral sling Alpha-blockers Anti-cholinergic medications 5-alpha reductase inhibitors Botox administration The correct answer is A, B. Stress incontinence is when there is urine leakage with increased abdominal pressure (lifting objects, laughing, sneezing, etc.). Which of the following management options is NOT appropriate for a patient with urinary stones composed of calcium oxalate? Calcium stones can either be calcium-phosphate stones or calcium-oxalate stones (more common). A physician recommends to a patient with urinary stones to increase the potassium citrate in his diet as blood pH alkalization is a key component of management and preventing further urinary stones. Which of the following urinary stones does this patient most likely have? Calcium-phosphate stones Calcium-oxalate stones Uric acid stones Magnesium ammonium phosphate stones Cystine stones The correct answer is C. This patient could have had uric acid stones or cystine stones, as both of these are treated with alkalinization of the urine. However, between these two, uric acid stones are more common (15%) than cystine stones (<1%)

Which of the following statements are true regarding urinary stones? Magnesium ammonium phosphate stones typically precipitate in an acidic pH Shockwave lithotripsy is an invasive procedure to remove stones Percutaneous nephrolithotomy is often indicated for large urinary stones including staghorn calculi Ureteroscopy is typically used to address stones in the renal pelvis and proximal ureter The correct answer is C. Struvite stones typically precipitate in a basic pH (phosphate precipitates in high pH and this often precipitated by urease producing organisms secreting ammonia in the urine). Shockwave lithotripsy uses shock waves to break up stones and is a non-invasive procedure. Ureter

You are a physician working a night shift in the emergency room when Robert comes in with severe left abdominal pain. Your suspicions of a kidney stone are confirmed with an ultrasound. You are waiting for some blood test results to determine the next course of treatment. Which test result is LEAST likely? Hyperuricemia Hypercalcemia Hypercitremia Hyperoxalemia Hyperphosphatemia The correct answer is C. Citrate is protective - it binds calcium preventing supersaturation of calcium, and it binds calcium oxalate crystals preventing crystal growth. If Robert had a kidney stone, he could have all of the remaining four options, and possibly hypocitremia.

Which of the following patients would be considered for a combined kidney pancreas transplant? A patient with kidney failure and Type 1 Diabetes A patient with kidney failure and Type 2 Diabetes A patient with kidney failure who is not yet on dialysis A patient with kidney failure who has been on dialysis for several years The correct answer is A. A combined kidney and pancreas transplant is a unique transplant where the patient with a failing kidney and Type 1 Diabetes gets both a pancreas and kidney. Type 1 Diabetes can contribute to failing kidney function – the addition of a pancreas transplant can address this co

Which of the following statements about hemodialysis (HD) and/or peritoneal dialysis (PD) is true? PD uses negative pressure to filter the blood Cardiovascular disease is a common complication of PD and HD HD is associated with better survival than PD PD is primarily done in hospital settings Patients receiving HD generally have a better quality of life than those receiving PD The correct answer is B. PD uses an osmotic gradient established by the peritoneum to filter blood, while hemodialysis uses negative pressure. Cardiovascular disease is a common complication of PD and HD and most patients with renal diseases often end up dying from cardiovascular reasons rather than

Which statement of kidney transplantation is true? Hemodialysis is preferred to kidney transplantation in most cases Transplantation requires immunosuppressants such as tacrolimus Type 2 diabetics qualify for a combined kidney/pancreas transplant Cadaveric donors are preferred over live donors The correct answer is B. Tacrolimus is a powerful immunosuppressant used in kidney transplantation. Kidney transplantation, compared with hemodialysis, is associated with better qualities of life and better 10-year survival. Live donors are preferred, but due to donor shortages, most transplants com

Robert has a kidney stone. Urinalysis results returned, indicating that it is made of calcium oxalate. Which of the following should be recommended to Robert for the management of his kidney stones? Select all that apply. Robert should drink more milk Robert should drink more red wine Robert should consume less oxalic acid in his diet Robert should increase his salt intake Robert should drink more fluids The correct answer is A, C, E. Calcium binds to oxalic acid in the digestive tract, prevent absorption. This increased dietary calcium would benefit patients with calcium oxalate kidney stones. Oxalic acid should be avoided if possible. Finally, increasing fluid-intake is always helpful in the case

Which of the following are criteria for “House’s Law”? Choose all that apply. Disorders of serum sodium are sodium handling problems Disorders of serum sodium are water handling problems Disorders of ECF volume are sodium handling problems Disorders of ECF volume are water handling problems The correct answer is B, C. Disorders of serum sodium are actually water handling problems, whereas ECF disorders are sodium handling problems.

Which of the following is true with respect to edema? Choose all that apply Generalized edema most often reflects cardiac, liver, or renal disease Edema represents volume contraction Widespread edema is called anasarca Can also present as ascites The correct answer is A, C, D. Edema usually presents with volume overload, which can be caused by cardiac, liver, or renal causes. Edema can also present as ascites in the abdomen.

Which of the following is true with respect to Anti-diuretic hormone is true? Choose all that apply. It is also called vasopressin It is released from the hypothalamus It is released in response to ECF volume contraction Increasing osmolality should shut down ADH production The correct answer is A, C. ADH is released from the posterior pituitary when osmolality is increasing, sensed by the hypothalamus. When osmolality begins to decline, ADH production is shut down.

What is false with respect to measured serum Na? It indicates how much water is in the ECF relative to Na Serum Osm = 2XNa + urea + K If true serum is high, then water is drawn from the ICF to the ECF Measuring serum Na is relatively cheap and reliable The correct answer is B. The formula for calculating Serum osmolality is = 2XNa + Urea +. GLUCOSE, not potassium.

What is true with respect to diabetes insipidus? It can be caused by trauma and infections It may result from the inadequate production of ADH It presents with passing large amounts of dilute, tasteless urine All of the above The correct answer is D. All the above are true. Diabetes insipidus is associated with increased thirst and drinking and may result from inadequate central production of ADH or inadequate renal response to ADH. It can be caused by injuries or trauma, most often brain injuries and post-op neurosurger

Which of the following are correct in terms of hyponatremia? In some cases, IV fluids hypertonic to urine should be given If symptomatic, treatment with fluids should be fast The underlying cause should be found and corrected Access to free water should NOT be restricted The correct answer is A, C. If symptomatic, the first few mmol/L should be done quickly, while the rest should be done at a slow rate. Access to free water should be restricted, and this can include restricting oral fluids, feeds, and some IV fluids)

You are working in the emergency room and a patient comes in with a serum potassium of 7.6. What is the FIRST thing you do? Inject patient with insulin Tell the patient to stop taking potassium supplements and reduce potassium in their diet The patient should be put on dialysis The patient should be injected with calcium gluconate to stabilize the cardiac membrane The correct answer is D. While the other options can help the patient in the long-term, the first immediate thing should be to give the patient calcium gluconate to stabilize the patient and prevent cardiacrelated death.

Potassium disorders can arise for many reasons. Which of the following is NOT one of the mechanisms by which these disorders arise? Intake Shift Output Conversion The correct answer is D. The 3 mechanisms are intake (diet, tissue necrosis), output (kidneys), and shift (through insulin or beta receptors, for example)

Which of the following is false in terms of regulating acids-bases in the kidney? The proximal tubule has carbonic anhydrase which facilitates reabsorption of bicarbonate The proximal tubule secretes H+ Excreted acid appears as ammonium in the urine The proximal tubule senses acidosis and increases bicarbonate reabsorption and ammonium secretion. The correct answer is B. The distal tubule secretes H+ by the alpha intercalated cells driven by aldosterone.

You are reading a patients’ ABG report. The patient has a pH of 7.7. The patient has a bicarbonate that has risen by 20 points above the normal. The pCO2 is also increased, but only by 14 points. Just based off this information, what is the likely condition the patient has? Metabolic acidosis Metabolic alkalosis Respiratory acidosis Respiratory alkalosis The correct answer is B. The patient’s pH is high, which means this is an alkalosis. Also, the compensation is as follows: bicarbonate: pCO2 is 10:7. Remember, you can breath a bit slower but your need for oxygen is a competing demand, so not quite 1:1 ratio for compensation.

What are some reasons to give a patient IV fluids? Treating ECF hypovolemia Treating ICF hypovolemia Provide nutrition Correct electrolyte disturbances A, B, and D All of the above The correct answer is F. All are valid reasons to give a patient IV fluids. From 13 - IV Fluids. The lecture's own (non-exhaustive) list of indications names every option: ECF hypovolemia (restore hemodynamics and tissue perfusion), ICF hypovolemia (free water to re-expand shrunken cells), replacing

How does D5W distribute? The glucose prevents hemolysis at the site of fluid administration, and water distributes 2/3 into the ICF, 1/3 into ECF The glucose prevents hemolysis at the site of fluid administration, and water distributes 1/3 into the ICF, and 2/3 into ECF The glucose prevents hemolysis at the site of fluid administration, and water distributes ½ into ICF and ½ into ECF None of the above The correct answer is A. D5W is essentially free water. The glucose prevents hemolysis at the site of administration, but is quickly metabolized, leaving water to distribute 2/3 into ICF and 1/3 into ECF.

The renal fascia is a membranous layer of connective tissue that encapsulates the kidneys, suprarenal glands and perirenal far. It does not cover the inferior portion of the kidneys though, leading to some individuals developing a condition where when stood up, the kidneys can descend up to 5 cm. This condition is called? Hydronephrosis Hyponephrosis Lithonephrosis Nephological decent Nephroptosis The correct answer is E. Nephroptosis is the condition where the renal fascia is weakened inferiorly leading to the kidneys descending when the individual in question stands up.

Which of the following list the order of renal blood flow in the correct order? For clarification, the order is to be listed from the larger arteries on the left, to the smaller more refined arteries to the right. Abdominal Aorta, renal artery, segmental artery, interlobar artery, arcuate artery, interlobular artery Abdominal Aorta, renal artery, interlobar artery, segmental artery, arcuate artery, interlobular artery Abdominal Aorta, renal artery, arcuate artery, interlobar artery, segmental artery, interlobular artery Abdominal Aorta, renal artery, interlobar artery, arcuate artery, segmental artery, interlobular artery Abdominal Aorta, renal artery, interlobular artery, interlobar artery, arcuate artery, segmental artery The correct answer is A. refer to diagrams regarding renal circulation for the best results. It can be confusing to differentiate between the interlobar and interlobular arteries.

The human embryo develops three kidney systems. Which of the following list their function correctly? The pronephros become the permanent adult set of kidneys and do not atrophy The mesonephros are the first kidney system to develop and provide early filtration for the developing embryo The metanephros become the permanent adult set of kidneys both the pronephros and metanephros atrophy C and D The correct answer is E. Both C and D are correct. Pro, and mesonephros atrophy in place of the final adult kidneys originating from the metanephros

A “fusion of the lower poles of the kidneys in the midline” best describes which developmental abnormality? erroneous renal atrophy bilateral renal agenesis Horseshoe kidneys bifid kidneys unilateral renal agenesis The correct answer is C. The kidneys have a chance to make contact on their ascent to their final location in the adult. Should they make contact before the inferior mesenteric artery their shape can get caught on it and stretch out to form a horseshoe shape.

Which of the following are primary kidney functions? Ion Regulation Osmoregulation waste management hormone production all of the above The correct answer is E. All of the listed functions are primary functions, one that is missing from the list is gluconeogenesis, which in times where it is needed the kidneys can make sugars to feed the rest of the body.

Which of the following are the basic functional units of the kidney? Collecting ducts renal pelvis proximal tubules distal tubules glomerulus The correct answer is E. Glomerular function is what is measured when nephron function is referenced.

Starling forces govern GFR in the kidneys. Which of the following starling forces are greatly depending on blood pressure above all else? interstitial fluid colloidal oncotic pressure capillary hydrostatic pressure capillary fluid colloidal oncotic pressure interstitial fluid hydrostatic pressure none of the above The correct answer is B. One could make the argument that each force is interdependent on each other. However, the force relying on blood pressure the most would be the capillary hydrostatic pressure.

The macula densa is located near which structure of the glomerulus? juxtaglomerular cells proximal collecting duct glomerulus renal pelvis none of the above The correct answer is A. The juxtaglomerular cells are located near the macula densa to communicate the osmotic conditions of the tubule.

Which of the following is true regarding the proximal tubule? it is approximately 15 mm long is devoid of any microvilli has a large surface area for the movement of solutes and the actions of carbonic anhydrase connects to the collecting duct directly A and C The correct answer is E. Both A and C are correct. The surface area arises from microvilli which aid in reabsorption.

Which of the following are true regarding the thick ascending limb? responsible for the reabsorption of electrolytes from the filtrate impervious to the movement of water responsive to look diuretics targeting the na-k-2cl transporter none of the above, these are the functions of the distal tubule A B and C The correct answer is E. A, B and C are all correct, From 06 - Reabsorption and Secretion. The thick ascending limb reabsorbs about 30% of the remaining filtered NaCl through the apical Na-K-2Cl cotransporter , and it is impermeable to water , which is how it dilutes the filtrate and builds the hype

What could be a potential complication of a proximal tubular disorder? respiratory acidosis metabolic acidosis glucosuria phosphaturia B C and D The correct answer is E. B, C and D are all correct, the proximal tubule is responsible for an array of absorption and secretion.

The mechanism behind k sparing diuretics is? blocking the K channel in the collecting duct so as to preserve K blocking the NaK ATPase enhancing the activity of the passive Na channel Blocking the passive Na channel none of the above The correct answer is D. The movement of Na passively into the cell leads to the excretion of K.

Which of the following regarding diuretics is correct: NSAIDs should be avoided/prescribed with caution to patients already taking furosemide, amiloride, or chlorthalidone spironolactone causes hyperkalemia and hypercalcemia loops diuretics can be used to treat recurrent calcium kidney stones triamterene is commonly used as a monotherapy to treat congestive heart failure A. i, ii B. i C. i, iii D. iii, iv E. None of the above i is the only correct option. NSAIDs should be avoided with these diuretics because NSAIDs impairs potassium and sodium excretion, which decreases the effect of loops diuretics and thiazide (furosemide, chlorthalidone), while also worsening hyperkalemia with K sparing diuretics (amiloride).
