Metatarsal squeeze Morton's neuroma Steps Squeeze the metatarsal heads together from the sides Positive Pain or a click in the web space ▶ Metatarsal Squeeze Test for Morton's Neuroma Tap to reveal
MSK exam, by region · Ottawa ankle and foot rules

Ottawa ankle and foot rules Who needs an X-ray (age 18 or over) Steps Press the back edge and tip of each malleolus (distal 6 cm of tibia and fibula) Press the base of the 5th metatarsal and the navicular Ask them to walk 4 steps Positive Any bony tenderness there , or cannot bear weight for 4 steps (right after the injury and in the emergency department) → X-ray ▶ Ottawa Ankle Rules Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Language (aphasia screen)

Language (aphasia screen) Types of dysphasia later: PoM 2 Neurology Steps Fluency : listen to their speech in answer to an open question Comprehension : a 3-step command ("Take this paper, fold it in half, put it on the floor") Naming : a pen, a watch, then their parts (the cap, the face) Repetition : "No ifs, ands or buts" Reading and writing : read a sentence aloud; write any sentence Positive Halting speech, understanding intact = expressive (Broca's) · fluent nonsense, poor understanding = receptive (Wernicke's) · everything lost = global · all normal but slurred = dysarthria , not aphasia (normal: fluent, follows commands, names, repeats) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN I, olfactory: smell

CN I, olfactory: smell Loss of smell later: PoM 2 Neurology Steps Patient closes the eyes and blocks one nostril Offer a familiar, non-irritating smell (coffee, soap) Ask them to name it Repeat on the other nostril Positive Cannot smell or identify it , one side or both (normal: identifies it each side) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN VIII, vestibulocochlear: hearing

CN VIII, vestibulocochlear: hearing Hearing Steps Block one ear; whisper numbers or rub your fingers by the other, out of sight If abnormal: Weber (512 Hz fork on top of the head) and Rinne (fork on the mastoid, then beside the ear) Positive Weber louder in the bad ear and Rinne bone louder than air = conductive · Weber louder in the good ear = sensorineural (normal: hears whisper; Weber central; Rinne air louder than bone) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN II, optic: visual acuity

CN II, optic: visual acuity Visual acuity Steps Distance glasses on (note them) Cover one eye; read the smallest line they can on the chart Repeat with the other eye Positive Reduced acuity in one or both eyes (normal: 20/20) ▶ Near Visual Acuity (1:16) ▶ Near Visual Acuity, view 2 (1:01) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN II: visual fields by confrontation

CN II: visual fields by confrontation Visual fields Steps Eye level, about an arm's length apart Patient covers one eye, you close your opposite eye; they look at your nose Bring a finger in from the edge in all four quadrants (or hold up fingers to count) Repeat for the other eye Positive Missed quadrant or field, or a blind spot (scotoma) (normal: sees the finger when you do) ▶ Testing Visual Fields (1:15) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN II and III: pupillary light reflex

CN II and III: pupillary light reflex Pupillary light reflex (II carries light in, III constricts the pupil) Steps Note pupil size, shape, symmetry Patient looks into the distance Light into one eye: watch direct and consensual constriction Repeat on the other eye Near reaction : follow your finger in toward the nose Positive Unequal, irregular, sluggish or absent response (normal: PERRLA, pupils equal, round, reactive to light and accommodation) ▶ Pupillary Light Response and RAPD (1:31) ▶ Cranial Nerve Exam Pupillary Light Response and RAPD (0:44) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN II: swinging light test

CN II: swinging light test Relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD) : one optic nerve later: PoM 2 Neurology Steps Dim light; patient looks into the distance Light in one eye for 2–3 seconds Swing quickly to the other eye Swing back and forth a few times Positive Both pupils dilate when the light swings onto one eye = RAPD in that eye (optic nerve, e.g. optic neuritis) (normal: both stay constricted) ▶ Pupillary Light Response and RAPD (1:31) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN II: fundoscopy

CN II: fundoscopy Optic disc and retina Steps Dim the room, ophthalmoscope dial at 0 Approach from about 15° to the side ; see the red reflex Follow a vessel to the optic disc Note disc margins, colour, cup-to-disc ratio , then vessels, retina and macula Positive Swollen disc with blurred margins (papilledema) , haemorrhages (normal: sharp margins, pale pink to yellow disc, cup less than half the disc, veins larger and darker than arteries) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN III, IV, VI: eye movements

CN III, IV, VI: eye movements Extraocular movement Steps Finger 45–60 cm away; head still , eyes follow Trace an "H" Ask about double vision Watch for nystagmus at the ends Positive Restricted movement, double vision, misalignment or nystagmus (normal: full movement, no diplopia) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN V, trigeminal: sensation

CN V, trigeminal: sensation Sensory function of the face Steps Patient closes the eyes Touch a cotton wisp to the forehead (V1), cheek (V2) and chin (V3) on each side Ask whether each side feels the same Positive Reduced or absent feeling in one branch or one side (normal: equal on both sides) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN V: motor

CN V: motor Motor function (muscles of chewing) Steps Feel the temporalis (temple) and masseter (jaw angle) on both sides Patient clenches the teeth Positive Weak or uneven contraction , wasting (normal: strong and equal) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN V and VII: corneal reflex

CN V and VII: corneal reflex The V and VII reflex: V carries the touch in, VII closes the eye Steps Usually offered rather than done in a teaching station: patient looks up and away Come in from the side, out of view Lightly touch the cornea with a cotton wisp Repeat on the other eye Positive No blink (normal: both eyes blink) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN VII, facial: motor

CN VII, facial: motor Motor function of facial expression Steps Raise the eyebrows Close the eyes tightly against your attempt to open them Smile, bare the teeth Puff out the cheeks Positive One side weak : whole side = lower motor neuron (for example Bell's palsy); lower face on the opposite side only, forehead spared = upper motor neuron (for example stroke) (normal: symmetric, strong) ▶ Facial Power Exam (CN VII) (0:27) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN VII: sensory
CN VII: sensory Sensory function: taste, front two-thirds of the tongue Steps Ask about any change in taste Positive Taste loss on one side of the front of the tongue Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN IX and X: palate

CN IX and X: palate Motor function Steps Listen to the voice and ask about swallowing Patient says "ahh" Watch the soft palate and uvula Positive Palate rises on one side only, uvula pulled to one side ; hoarse voice (normal: symmetric rise, uvula midline) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN IX and X: gag reflex

CN IX and X: gag reflex Gag reflex Steps Usually offered rather than done in a teaching station: tell the patient first Lightly touch the back of the throat on each side with a tongue depressor Positive No gag on one side or both (normal: gag on each side); not done routinely, mostly to check airway protection or the brainstem Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN XI, spinal accessory

CN XI, spinal accessory Motor function of the trapezius and sternocleidomastoid Steps Look for wasting or asymmetry of the neck and shoulders Shrug against your resistance Turn the head to each side against your hand Positive Weakness or wasting on one side (normal: strong, equal) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · CN XII, hypoglossal

CN XII, hypoglossal Motor function of the tongue Steps Look at the tongue resting in the mouth : wasting, fasciculations Stick the tongue straight out Move it side to side; push it into each cheek against your finger Positive Tongue deviates toward the weak side , wasting, fasciculations, weak push (normal: midline, strong) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Pronator drift

Pronator drift Subtle upper motor neuron weakness of the arm later: PoM 2 Neurology Steps Arms straight out in front, palms up Eyes closed Hold for about 20–30 seconds Watch each arm Positive One arm turns palm-down (pronates) and drifts down = upper motor neuron weakness on that side (normal: both arms stay level, palms up) ▶ Pronator Drift (0:46) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Shoulder abduction

Shoulder abduction Shoulder power: C5 , axillary nerve (deltoid, supraspinatus) Steps Arms out to the sides, elbows bent "Don't let me push down" Push down above the elbow Positive Weakness , one side or both (normal: 5/5) ▶ Strength Testing Shoulder Abduction (0:21) ▶ Strength Testing Shoulder Abduction, view 2 (0:17) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Elbow flexion

Elbow flexion Elbow power: C5–C6 , musculocutaneous nerve (biceps, brachialis) Steps Elbow bent 90°, palm up "Pull me toward you" Resist at the wrist Positive Weakness ▶ Strength Testing Elbow Flexion - Biceps (0:24) ▶ Strength Testing Elbow Flexion - Biceps, view 2 (0:20) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Elbow extension

Elbow extension Elbow power: C6–C8 (mainly C7 ), radial nerve (triceps) Steps Elbow bent "Push me away" Resist at the wrist Positive Weakness ▶ Strength Testing Elbow Extension (0:16) ▶ Strength Testing Elbow Extension, view 2 (0:02) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Wrist extension

Wrist extension Wrist power: C6–C7 , radial nerve (wrist extensors) extra Steps Make a fist, wrist cocked up "Don't let me push it down" Push down on the back of the hand Positive Weakness (wrist drop in a radial nerve palsy) ▶ Strength Testing Wrist Extension (0:09) ▶ Strength Testing Wrist Extension, view 2 (0:17) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Finger abduction

Finger abduction Finger power: C8–T1 , ulnar nerve (interossei) Steps Fingers spread wide "Don't let me push them together" Squeeze the index and little fingers in Positive Weakness ▶ Strength Testing Finger Abduction (0:14) ▶ Strength Testing Finger Abduction, view 2 (0:34) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Grip strength
Grip strength Grip: screens C6–T1 Steps Patient squeezes two of your fingers Compare sides Positive Weak grip Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Hip flexion
Hip flexion Hip power: L2–L4 , femoral nerve (iliopsoas) Steps Seated or lying, lift the thigh Push down on the thigh Positive Weakness Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Knee extension
Knee extension Knee power: L2–L4 , femoral nerve (quadriceps) Steps Knee bent "Kick out straight" Resist at the shin Positive Weakness Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Knee flexion
Knee flexion Knee power: L4–S2 , sciatic nerve (hamstrings) Steps Knee bent "Pull your heel back" Resist at the back of the ankle Positive Weakness Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Ankle dorsiflexion
Ankle dorsiflexion Ankle power: L4–L5 , deep peroneal nerve (tibialis anterior) Steps "Pull your foot up toward your face" Resist on top of the foot Positive Weakness (foot drop) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Ankle plantar flexion
Ankle plantar flexion Ankle power: S1 , tibial nerve (gastrocnemius, soleus) Steps "Push your foot down like on a gas pedal" Resist under the ball of the foot Positive Weakness Tap to reveal

Pain (pinprick) Pain (spinothalamic) Steps Use a clean sharp object and a dull one Patient says " sharp " or " dull " Compare sides and distal with proximal Positive Cannot tell sharp, or feels it less , in a pattern (normal: equal, correct each time) ▶ Pinprick C6 (0:01) ▶ Pinprick C7 (0:04) ▶ Pinprick C8 (0:04) ▶ Pinprick L3-S1 (0:26) Tap to reveal

Temperature Temperature (spinothalamic) Steps Touch the skin with a cool tuning fork Ask " hot or cold? " and "is it the same as here?" Positive Reduced or absent sense of cold ▶ Sensory Exam: Normal (NeuroLogic Exam) (Eccles Health Sciences Library (Univ. of Utah)) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Light touch
Light touch Light touch Steps Cotton wisp , no pressure Patient says "yes" each time they feel it Compare areas Positive Missed touches in a pattern Tap to reveal

Vibration Vibration (dorsal columns) Steps Strike a 128 Hz fork; show it on the forehead Place it on the last joint of the index finger (your finger underneath) and the big toe joint Patient says when they feel it and when it stops If lost, move up to the next bony point ( start distally, move proximally ) Positive Feels it stop early, or not at all , usually at the toes first (normal: feels it until you do) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Proprioception (joint position)

Proprioception (joint position) Proprioception (dorsal columns) Steps Hold the end of the finger or big toe by its sides Show "up" and "down" Eyes closed: move it up or down in a random order Positive Wrong answers (normal: correct each time) Tap to reveal

Stereognosis Cortical sensation Steps Eyes closed Put a familiar object (coin, key) in the hand Ask them to name it Positive Cannot name it although primary sensation is intact → parietal (sensory cortex) Tap to reveal

Graphesthesia Cortical sensation Steps Eyes closed Draw a number on the palm with a blunt tip Ask them to name it Positive Cannot name it although primary sensation is intact → parietal (sensory cortex) ▶ Sensory Exam: Normal (NeuroLogic Exam) (Eccles Health Sciences Library (Univ. of Utah)) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Extinction (both sides at once)

Extinction (both sides at once) Parietal lobe syndrome: sensory neglect later: PoM 2 Neurology Steps Eyes closed Touch one hand, then the other: "Which side?" Then touch both at once Visual version: wiggle fingers in both fields at once Positive Feels each side alone but misses one side when both are touched together → parietal (visual extinction → occipital) (normal: "both") Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Two-point discrimination

Two-point discrimination Cortical sensation (fine touch) extra Steps Eyes closed Touch the fingertip with one or two points of an opened paper clip Ask "one or two?" Narrow the gap until they cannot tell Positive Needs a wider gap than the other side (normal fingertip: about 2–5 mm) ▶ Sensory Exam: Normal (NeuroLogic Exam) (Eccles Health Sciences Library (Univ. of Utah)) Tap to reveal

Biceps C5–C6 (mainly C5) Steps Arm relaxed, elbow bent Thumb on the biceps tendon in the elbow crease Tap your thumb Positive Absent, reduced, very brisk or unequal (normal: elbow flexes, equal both sides) ▶ Biceps Reflex Sitting (0:26) Tap to reveal

Brachioradialis C5–C6 (mainly C6) Steps Forearm resting, thumb up Tap the thumb side of the forearm , a few centimetres above the wrist Positive Absent, reduced, very brisk or unequal (normal: forearm flexes and turns slightly) ▶ Brachioradialis Reflex Sitting (0:12) Tap to reveal

Triceps C6–C7 (mainly C7) Steps Arm across the body or hanging, elbow bent Tap the triceps tendon just above the point of the elbow Positive Absent, reduced, very brisk or unequal (normal: elbow extends) ▶ Tricep Reflex Sitting (0:07) ▶ Tricep Reflex Sitting, view 2 (0:08) ▶ Tricep Reflex Sitting, view 3 (0:03) ▶ Tricep Reflex Sitting, view 4 (0:53) Tap to reveal

Knee (patellar) L2–L4 (mainly L4) Steps Patient seated, legs dangling (or knees supported) Tap the tendon just below the kneecap Positive Absent, reduced, very brisk or unequal (normal: knee extends) ▶ Knee Reflex Sitting (0:24) Tap to reveal

Ankle (Achilles) S1–S2 (mainly S1) Steps Foot gently pushed up (dorsiflexed) Tap the Achilles tendon above the heel Positive Absent, reduced, very brisk or unequal (normal: foot plantar flexes) ▶ Ankle Reflex Sitting (0:33) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Plantar response

Plantar response L5–S1 , upper motor neuron sign (not a tendon reflex) Steps With a blunt point, stroke the outer edge of the sole from the heel toward the toes Then across the ball of the foot Positive Big toe goes up and the other toes fan out (Babinski sign) = upper motor neuron lesion (normal: toes curl down) ▶ Plantar Response (0:02) ▶ Plantar Response Test (0:16) ▶ Plantar Response Test, view 2 (0:58) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Ankle clonus

Ankle clonus Upper motor neuron sign, when the reflexes are brisk later: PoM 2 Neurology Steps Knee slightly bent, supported Sharply push the foot up (dorsiflex) and hold it there Count the beats Positive Repeated rhythmic beats of the foot (more than a few) = clonus = upper motor neuron lesion (normal: none, or 1–2 beats that stop) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Rapid alternating movements

Rapid alternating movements Cerebellar function: dysdiadochokinesia Steps Hands : patient flips one hand palm up, palm down on the other palm or thigh as fast as they can Feet : taps the foot on the floor or your hand quickly Each side in turn Positive Slow, clumsy, irregular alternation (dysdiadochokinesia) (normal: fast, even rhythm) Tap to reveal

Finger-nose Cerebellar function: dysmetria and intention tremor Steps Hold your finger at arm's length Patient touches your finger, then their nose , back and forth Move your finger between touches Positive Overshoots or misses (dysmetria) , tremor worse near the target (intention tremor) (normal: smooth and accurate) Tap to reveal

Heel-shin Cerebellar function in the legs Steps Patient lying down Place one heel on the opposite knee Slide it down the shin to the ankle, and back Each side Positive Heel wobbles or falls off the shin (normal: smooth, stays on the shin) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Tandem gait
Tandem gait Ataxia Steps Walk in a straight line heel to toe Stand close by Positive Cannot keep the line, steps off or sways (normal: steady) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Romberg test

Romberg test Sensory ataxia (lost joint position sense) vs cerebellar ataxia later: PoM 2 Neurology Steps Patient stands with feet together , eyes open Stand close to catch them Patient closes the eyes (up to about 60 seconds) Watch for swaying or falling Positive Steady with eyes open but sways or falls with eyes closed = positive Romberg = sensory ataxia (dorsal columns or nerves: B12 deficiency, peripheral neuropathy) · unsteady even with eyes open = cerebellar ataxia (Romberg not positive) (normal: steady both ways) Tap to reveal

Cortex Weakness on one side, face and arm more than leg (upper motor neuron) Steps Upper motor neuron signs on one side Look for a cortical sign : aphasia (dominant side), neglect (non-dominant side), a homonymous hemianopia Check cortical sensation: stereognosis, graphesthesia, extinction Positive Any one cortical sign puts it in the cortex · e.g. left middle cerebral artery (MCA) stroke: right face and arm weaker than leg, plus expressive aphasia Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Subcortex (white matter, internal capsule)

Subcortex (white matter, internal capsule) One side, face, arm and leg alike Steps Upper motor neuron signs on one side No cortical signs Is it pure motor, pure sensory, or mild weakness with mild clumsiness on the same side? Positive Pure motor or pure sensory hemibody, or ataxic hemiparesis, with no cortical signs · internal capsule: motor and sensory together Tap to reveal

Brainstem Upper motor neuron weakness plus cranial nerve findings Steps Upper motor neuron signs Vertigo, or double vision, plus another symptom Is sensation crossed (face on one side, body on the other)? Positive Crossed signs, or cranial nerve findings with long-tract signs Tap to reveal

Cerebellum Coordination , not power Steps Listen to the speech: slurred? Watch the eyes: nystagmus? Finger-nose, rapid alternating movements, heel-shin Gait and tandem walking Positive Ataxia on the same side as the lesion, power normal · e.g. slurred speech plus right finger-nose ataxia → right cerebellum Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Spinal cord

Spinal cord Both legs (paraparesis) or all four limbs (quadriparesis) , upper motor neuron Steps Upper motor neuron signs below the lesion: brisk reflexes, upgoing toes Find a sensory level Ask about bladder and bowel Ask about neck or back pain Positive Upper motor neuron signs in both legs (or all four limbs) plus a sensory level · cervical cord → all four limbs, thoracic → legs · e.g. cervical spondylosis Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Anterior horn cell

Anterior horn cell Weakness that varies, upper and lower motor neuron signs together Steps Wasting and fasciculations (lower motor neuron) Brisk reflexes in the same limbs (upper motor neuron) Test sensation Positive Both kinds of motor neuron signs, sensation normal · e.g. amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Nerve root

Nerve root One myotome , lower motor neuron Steps Weakness only in that root's muscles That root's reflex reduced Pinprick in that dermatome Ask about neck or back pain shooting down the limb Positive Myotomal weakness, dermatomal sensory loss and the matching reflex reduced, with pain · e.g. disc herniation (radiculopathy) Tap to reveal

Plexus One limb, several nerves , lower motor neuron Steps Weakness across more than one nerve and root in one limb Sensory loss in that limb Ask about pain Positive One limb, more than one nerve, usually painful · e.g. brachial neuritis Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Peripheral nerve

Peripheral nerve One nerve's muscles, or distal more than proximal on both sides Steps Weakness in one nerve's area, or feet before hands Sensory loss in that nerve, or glove and stocking Ankle reflexes Positive Single nerve, or length-dependent: feet first, glove-and-stocking loss, ankle jerks reduced or absent · e.g. Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) Tap to reveal
Neurological exam, top down · Neuromuscular junction

Neuromuscular junction Eyes first, then speech and swallowing ; fluctuates Steps Droopy lids (ptosis), double vision Does weakness worsen with use ? Test sensation and reflexes Positive Fatigable, descending weakness, eyes first, with normal sensation and reflexes · e.g. myasthenia gravis Tap to reveal

Muscle Proximal and symmetric : shoulder and hip girdle, neck, trunk Steps Trouble rising from a chair, climbing stairs, lifting the arms Test sensation Test reflexes Positive Proximal symmetric weakness, no sensory loss, reflexes often normal · e.g. dermatomyositis Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Clubbing (Schamroth sign)

Clubbing (Schamroth sign) Chronic lung disease (also heart and gut disease) Steps Ask the patient to put the backs of the two index fingertips together , nail to nail Look for the small diamond-shaped window between the nails Positive Diamond window lost · early clubbing: soft, spongy nail bed (normal: a diamond-shaped gap) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Asterixis

Asterixis CO2 retention (too much carbon dioxide in the blood) or liver failure (encephalopathy) Steps Arms straight out in front Bend the wrists back , like stopping traffic Hold for a few seconds Positive Flapping tremor of the hands ▶ Examination for asterixis (Top Hat Tutorials) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Capillary refill

Capillary refill Poor perfusion (blood flow to the fingers) extra Steps Hold the patient's hand at about heart level Press a fingernail firmly for 5 seconds until the nail bed goes pale Let go and count how long the pink returns Positive Colour takes longer than 2 seconds to return (normal: under 2 seconds ) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Tracheal position

Tracheal position Something pulling or pushing the trachea Steps Inspect first: is the trachea midline? Place your fingers along one side of the trachea and feel the space between it and the sternocleidomastoid muscle Compare with the other side Positive Unequal spaces · toward the bad side: atelectasis, fibrosis, lung collapse · away : pleural effusion, hemothorax (blood), tension pneumothorax (normal: equal spaces, midline) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes

Cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes Enlarged nodes ( lymphadenopathy ): infection, or a lung cancer that has spread later: Respirology Steps Patient sitting , you in front or behind With the pads of two or three fingers , roll gently over the neck chains (in front of and behind the sternocleidomastoid, under the jaw, behind the ear) Then press into the hollow above each collarbone (supraclavicular) Compare both sides Positive Enlarged, firm or fixed nodes , especially above the collarbone (normal: not palpable, or small, soft and mobile) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Chest shape and skin (SEADS)

Chest shape and skin (SEADS) Deformity or hyperinflation , scars, skin change Steps Look at the whole chest from the front, the side and the back Compare the front-to-back (AP) diameter with the side-to-side one Run through SEADS : swelling, erythema, atrophy, deformities, scars Positive Barrel chest (AP as wide as side-to-side) · pectus excavatum or carinatum · kyphosis or scoliosis · scars or wasting (normal: AP narrower than side-to-side, no deformity) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Respiratory movement and accessory muscles

Respiratory movement and accessory muscles Work of breathing ; one side not moving Steps Ask for a few deep breaths Watch both sides together for one side lagging Look at the neck and between the ribs for accessory muscle use Positive One side lags · neck muscles contract or skin sucks in between the ribs (normal: both sides rise together, no accessory muscles at rest) ▶ Stigmata of COPD: chest shape, accessory muscles (Stanford Medicine 25) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Spine and renal angle tenderness

Spine and renal angle tenderness Bone or kidney problem Steps Warn the patient With the side of your fist , gently thump down the spinous processes Then each renal angle (where the lowest rib meets the back muscles) Positive Spine tender : tuberculosis (TB) or tumour · renal angle tender : kidney infection (pyelonephritis) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Chest expansion

Chest expansion Asymmetry or reduced movement Steps Hands on the lower back at the level of the 10th ribs Slide thumbs toward the spine, raising a loose fold of skin between them Ask for a deep breath Watch your thumbs Positive Thumbs move apart unequally , or barely at all (normal: equal, symmetrical movement) ▶ Chest expansion (respiratory exam) (Geeky Medics) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Tactile fremitus

Tactile fremitus What lies under the chest wall: solid, fluid or air Steps Arms crossed Use the ball of the palm or the ulnar (little-finger) edge of one hand Patient says "ninety-nine" or "boy-oh-boy" each time you touch Work down the back side to side , comparing matching spots Positive Increased : consolidation (pneumonia) · decreased on one side : atelectasis, pleural effusion, pneumothorax · decreased both sides : COPD, effusions on both sides (normal: equal on both sides; strongest between the shoulder blades) ▶ Tactile fremitus (WVSOM Academic) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Percussing a lung field

Percussing a lung field Air vs fluid vs solid under that spot Steps Press the middle finger of your non-dominant hand firmly on the chest, only its last joint (DIP) touching With the tip of your dominant middle finger , strike that joint twice , a quick relaxed flick from the wrist Pull back at once so you don't damp the sound Same level on the other side, then move down Positive Dull / flat or hyperresonant / tympanic (table below) (normal: resonant , equal both sides) ▶ Percussion of the lungs (Geeky Medics) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Diaphragmatic excursion

Diaphragmatic excursion How far the diaphragm moves Steps Patient breathes all the way out and holds : percuss down to where resonance turns dull; mark it Patient breathes all the way in and holds : find the new level; mark it Measure between the marks Positive Reduced movement (normal: 3-5 cm ; 7-8 cm can be normal in a well-conditioned person) later: PoM 1 Respirology Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Auscultating a lung field

Auscultating a lung field Intensity and character of breath sounds, and extra sounds Steps Patient sits, arms crossed , and breathes deeply through an open mouth Diaphragm of the stethoscope on bare skin between the ribs Listen to a full breath in and out at each spot Go side to side at the same level, apex to base (about 6 levels each side) Positive Bronchial sounds over the lung , decreased breath sounds, crackles or wheezes (normal: vesicular , equal both sides) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Egophony
Egophony Consolidation Steps Stethoscope over the suspicious area Patient says "eee" Positive "eee" sounds like "aaa" (normal: "eee" stays "eee") Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Whispered pectoriloquy
Whispered pectoriloquy Consolidation Steps Stethoscope over the suspicious area Patient whispers "one, two, three" Positive Whisper heard loud and clear (normal: faint and muffled) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Anterior percussion

Anterior percussion Air vs fluid vs solid in the front lung fields Steps Same finger technique as the back Start above and below the clavicles Move down the 2nd-4th spaces in the mid-clavicular line , then the lower chest in the anterior axillary line (about 5 spots each side) Compare each spot with the same level on the other side Positive Dull or hyperresonant (normal: resonant , equal both sides) ▶ Lung percussion (respiratory exam) (Geeky Medics) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Anterior auscultation

Anterior auscultation Intensity and character of breath sounds, extra sounds Steps Diaphragm of the stethoscope on bare skin, patient breathing deeply through an open mouth Same spots as percussion, side to side Listen to a full breath in and out at each spot Positive Bronchial sounds over the lung , decreased breath sounds, crackles or wheezes (normal: vesicular ) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Right middle lobe

Right middle lobe A lobe you cannot reach from the back Steps Find the right 4th-6th ribs , between the mid-clavicular and anterior axillary lines Percuss there, then auscultate there Positive Dull , or crackles or bronchial breathing (normal: resonant and vesicular) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Clubbing (upper limb)

Clubbing (upper limb) Chronic lung disease Steps Patient sitting or standing, both hands in view Schamroth sign : put the backs of the two index fingertips together , nail to nail Look for the diamond-shaped window and feel for a spongy nail bed Positive Diamond window lost (normal: a diamond-shaped gap) Tap to reveal
Respiratory exam, front to back · Pitting edema (lower limbs)

Pitting edema (lower limbs) Fluid in the legs: right-sided heart failure, which lung disease can cause Steps Patient sitting or standing , look at both ankles and shins Press a thumb firmly over the inner shin bone (tibia) or behind the ankle bone for about 5 seconds Let go and look for a dent Compare both legs Positive A dent that stays (pitting), one or both sides (normal: skin springs back at once) Tap to reveal
Vital signs and general inspection · Central cyanosis
Central cyanosis Low blood oxygen from lung or heart disease Steps Look at the lips Look inside the mouth and under the tongue Positive Blue lips and tongue Tap to reveal
Vital signs and general inspection · Peripheral cyanosis
Peripheral cyanosis Poor blood flow to the hands and feet Steps Look at the fingers and toes Positive Blue fingers and toes Tap to reveal
Vital signs and general inspection · Pallor

Pallor Anemia Steps Gently pull down the lower lid and look at the conjunctiva Look inside the mouth, at the nail beds and the palm creases Positive Pale (the inner rim of the lower lid is not red) Tap to reveal
Vital signs and general inspection · Plethora
Plethora Redness, e.g. from inflammation Steps Look at the skin wherever it shows Positive Red skin ▶ Plethora face: causes (Medicine Handy Points) Tap to reveal
Vital signs and general inspection · Jaundice

Jaundice Yellowing from bilirubin (e.g. liver disease) Steps Ask the patient to look up Gently pull down the lower lid Look at the whites of the eyes Positive Yellow whites of the eyes (scleral icterus) Tap to reveal
Vital signs and general inspection · Radial pulse

Radial pulse Rate, rhythm, amplitude, contour, symmetry Steps Index and middle finger pads on the radial artery Count for 15-30 seconds (×4 or ×2 = beats per minute) Rhythm : regular, regularly irregular, or irregularly irregular? Amplitude (strength): normal, decreased or increased? Contour (shape): upstroke and downstroke, single or double peak? Feel the other wrist and compare Positive Under 60 = bradycardia · over 100 = tachycardia · irregular · weak or bounding · unequal sides (normal: 60-100 , regular, normal amplitude, single peak, equal) Tap to reveal
Vital signs and general inspection · Counting the respiratory rate

Counting the respiratory rate Rate, rhythm, depth, effort Steps Keep your fingers on the radial pulse Watch the chest rise without telling the patient (breathing changes when people know they're being watched) Count for 15-30 seconds and multiply up Positive Too slow = bradypnea · too fast = tachypnea · irregular, shallow or laboured (normal adult: 14-20 breaths per minute , regular, effortless) Tap to reveal
Vital signs and general inspection · Palpated systolic estimate

Palpated systolic estimate Where to pump the cuff to Steps Feel the radial pulse Inflate quickly until the pulse disappears Add 30 mmHg : this is your target pressure Deflate fully Positive Sets the target, so you don't pump painfully high and don't miss the auscultatory gap (a silent stretch heard in some patients with high blood pressure or aortic stenosis) Tap to reveal
Vital signs and general inspection · Auscultated blood pressure

Auscultated blood pressure Systolic and diastolic pressure Steps Bell lightly over the brachial artery (Korotkoff sounds are low-pitched ) Inflate quickly to the target Deflate about 2-3 mmHg per second First Korotkoff sound = systolic Keep going: sounds disappear = diastolic ; listen a little lower to be sure Deflate to zero; report to the nearest 2 mmHg Repeat on the other arm Positive Office reading 130/80 or more → confirm outside the office (home or ambulatory monitoring) before calling it hypertension (normal: about 120/80 ; 5-10 mmHg difference between arms can be normal ) Tap to reveal
Vital signs and general inspection · Orthostatic blood pressure

Orthostatic blood pressure Orthostatic hypotension Steps Patient lying down for at least 5 minutes , then measure Patient stands ; measure again after 1-3 minutes (support the arm at heart level) Positive Systolic drops 20 mmHg or more, or diastolic drops 10 mmHg or more , from lying to standing Tap to reveal
